The series "Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems" publishes the latest developments in Networks and Systems-quickly, informally and with high quality. Original research reported in proceedings and post-proceedings represents the core of LNNS.

Volumes published in LNNS embrace all aspects and subﬁelds of, as well as new challenges in, Networks and Systems.

The series contains proceedings and edited volumes in systems and networks, spanning the areas of Cyber-Physical Systems, Autonomous Systems, Sensor Networks, Control Systems, Energy Systems, Automotive Systems, Biological Systems, Vehicular Networking and Connected Vehicles, Aerospace Systems, Automation, Manufacturing, Smart Grids, Nonlinear Systems, Power Systems, Robotics, Social Systems, Economic Systems and other. Of particular value to both the contributors and the readership are the short publication timeframe and the worldwide distribution and exposure which enable both a wide and rapid dissemination of research output.

The series covers the theory, applications, and perspectives on the state of the art and future developments relevant to systems and networks, decision making, control, complex processes and related areas, as embedded in the ﬁelds of interdisciplinary and applied sciences, engineering, computer science, physics, economics, social, and life sciences, as well as the paradigms and methodologies behind them.

Indexed by SCOPUS, EI Compendex, INSPEC, WTI Frankfurt eG, zbMATH, SCImago.

All books published in the series are submitted for consideration in Web of Science.

We are delighted to announce that The Second International Conference on Artiﬁcial Intelligence and Networking (ICAIN 2025) was proudly organized by BITS Pilani, Dubai Campus, in association with the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad, and Universal Innovator, on 6-7 October 2025 in Hybrid Mode. ## Synergistic Fusion of Physics-Informed

**and Data- Driven Deep Learning: A Hybrid ** **Multi-Task Framework for Advanced Battery ** **Fault Diagnosis and Prognosis **

## Sankaramurthy Padmini ( B ), Jeetham Chinni Krishna, and Amit Amol Jadhav

Department of Computing Technologies, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur, 603203 Chennai, India \{padminis,jc1102,aj9938\}@srmist.edu.in

**Abstract. ** The fast development of New Energy Vehicles (NEVs) highlights the signiﬁcance of all-around health monitoring systems that guarantee safety, reliability, and sustainability. In this paper, a hybrid multi-task deep learning framework that can perform single-shot fault classiﬁcation, risk score regression, and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation from raw sensor data is proposed. The framework utilizes a physics-informed loss function to guarantee monotonic risk behavior with temperature, thereby enhancing interpretability and compliance with physical laws. To assess predictive uncertainty, Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout is employed during inference. For interpretability, SHAP-based feature attribution is employed to identify signiﬁcant sensor features inﬂuencing predictions. Experimental results on a simulated NEV fault dataset show outstanding performance in terms of both accuracy and interpretability. The suggested framework is lightweight in weight and can be deployed on edge devices, hence enabling real-time diagnosis in NEVs. The hybrid multi-task deep learning approach shall be made robust by the collective classiﬁcation of faults, RUL prediction, and risk scoring using shared representation, facilitating the learning of inter-task interdependencies and thereby improved diagnostic accuracy and efﬁciency. Although the lightweight nature subsequently facilitates real-time inference on an edge device for NEV health monitoring.

**Keywords: ** New Energy Vehicles (NEVs) · Multi-task Learning · Remaining Useful Life (RUL) · Fault Classiﬁcation · Risk Score Prediction · PhysicsInformed Loss · Deep Learning · SHAP Interpretability · Uncertainty Estimation · Monte Carlo(MC) Dropout

## 1 **Introduction **

## Electric vehicle engineering is fast being propelled ahead by the demand for sustainable

and intelligent mobility around the world. EVs operate with sensitive electromechanical subsystems-motors, batteries, and power electronics-that respond greatly to temperature, vibration, and other variables. Small deviations may lead to a major failure if left unnoticed; thus, intelligent health-monitoring installations have become necessary.

© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026 - Virdee et al. (Eds.): ICAIN 2025, LNNS 1931, pp. 1-12, 2026.  <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-23314-1\_1> - Padmini et al.

One drawback with the conventional approaches to diagnostics and prognostics is that isolated tasks, such as fault classiﬁcation or RUL prediction, are addressed, which do not reﬂect the interconnected nature of system health. For this, we propose a hybrid multitask deep learning framework that classiﬁes faults, estimates RUL, and performs risk prediction simultaneously. It uses a shared encoder with task-speciﬁc heads, which, in turn, enhances generalization, robustness, and efﬁciency. Skip connections and modularity further enhance deep feature learning.

Apart from multi-tasking, the proposed approach integrates different ingredients comprising the bridge between AI and physical reliability: Physics-informed loss enforces monotonic risk predictions, SHAP enhances interpretability by explaining feature attributions, and Monte Carlo Dropout provides uncertainty metrics, especially for RUL. In all, it makes a scalable and interpretable system suitable for smart EV diagnostics. **1.1 ** **Main Contributions **

- Designed a hybrid multi-task deep learning framework that jointly performs fault  classiﬁcation, RUL prediction, and risk score prediction. - Designed a physics-informed loss function that ensures physical consistency and  interpretability. - Utilized Monte Carlo Dropout for the estimation of predictive uncertainty, essential  in safety-critical applications. - SHAP-based feature attribution is applied for improved transparency and actionable  decision-making. - Designed a lightweight architecture for NEV on edge, deployable in real time.

## 2 **Literature Survey **

In general, research in the domain of fault detection and RUL estimation applied to NEV systems has juggled how to bring together deep learning together with physicsbased methods. In Papers \[ 1 - 3 \], only deep-learning architectures have been proposed like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs), or hybrid models that classify fault conditions or predict RUL based purely on sensor readings. While these approaches can be seen to work reasonably well as isolated solution methods, they do not fully encompass physics-based principles nor account for the uncertainties of their own predictions.

Arias Chao et al. \[ 1 \] develop a hybrid framework that integrates both the physicsbased and data-driven approaches to enhance the prognosis of fault detection and RUL estimation in NEVs. Building on these lines, Muthukumar G and Jyosna Philip \[ 2 \] put forward a CNN-LSTM hybrid model combining the power of several learning techniques to describe the temporal dependencies of the sensor data in order to bolster the RUL prediction accuracy. Following a related path, Xu Zhaoyi, Guo Yanjie, and Saleh Joseph Homer \[ 3 \] present the notion of coupling deep learning and nonstationary Gaussian processes for prediction. This way, they achieve reliable prognosis results and provide credible conﬁdence intervals, which is crucial for maintenance-oriented Synergistic Fusion of Physics-Informed and Data- Driven Deep

Liu \[ 16 \] applied deep learning to the RUL prediction of aero-engines. Their proposed models had good generalization and scalability, both very suitable characteristics for application in NEV systems. Xie et al. \[ 10, 17 \] developed a CNN-LSTM hybrid deep learning-based prognostic model. It possessed both local feature extraction and long-term dependencies, aiming to enhance the prediction reliability by capturing both.

Similarly, Qiu et al. \[ 11, 18 \] reviewed in detail intelligent fault diagnosis for industrial equipment using deep learning, identiﬁed the strengths and weaknesses of different architectures, and pointed out the work on interpretability and robustness that still needs to be done regarding NEV fault diagnostics. Paper \[ 12 \] dealt with AI-based recommendations that enhance transparency and reproducibility, whereas paper \[ 19 \] proposed an ensemble hybrid deep learning model that enhances RUL estimation accuracy by fusing predictions across different models, tackling the problem of model bias and overﬁtting. In their subsequent work, de la Iglesia et al. \[ 13 \] further investigated loss-attentional PINNs, offering theoretical insight and empirical support for embedding physical constraints into deep learning workﬂows for NEV systems. Zhao et al. \[ 14 \] extended this line of review to sensor-based systems and emphasized the importance of data fusion and the management of prediction uncertainty in battery-powered applications. Li, Ma, and Yan \[ 20 \] proposed an early warning system using deep learning for the power battery in NEVs. Their system focuses on real-time health assessment and actionable fault detection. Li et al. applied the NARX neural network for fault diagnosis of batteries in an earlier work. It performed very well for real-time applications while maintaining low computational complexity, which is an important aspect in an embedded NEV environment \[ 21 \].

Other recent works also focus on attention-based architectures and uncertainty-aware models for fault prediction in safety-critical EV systems. Chen et al. \[ 22 \] proposed an attention-based hybrid model for concurrent fault and RUL estimation, while Gupta and Singh \[ 23, 24 \] introduced a Bayesian deep-learning setup quantifying predictive conﬁdence for the EV battery health diagnostics. These approaches therefore complement the focus of our framework on interpretability, uncertainty quantiﬁcation, and multitask learning. - Padmini et al.

## 3 **Proposed Methodology **

The proposed electric vehicle health monitoring framework is comprehensive, accurate, and easy to deploy. Deep learning, physics-based inference, uncertainty quantiﬁcation, and interpretability all ﬁt into a single framework. The proposed system performs three major tasks simultaneously: fault classiﬁcation, RUL estimation, and risk detection. Overall, the proposed scheme is divided into six main components, each of which contributes to enhancing the solution's robustness and applicability. **3.1 ** **Preprocessing of Data and Feature Engineering **

The unprocessed sensor readings from the motor temperature, voltage, vibration, current, and speed for various EV subsystems are cleaned and normalized using the Z-score normalization technique to have a uniform feature scale and handling missing values accordingly. Then, small volumes of Gaussian noise are added to the numeric features for augmentation, thereby enhancing generalization. Finally, the augmented dataset is split into a training set and a test set with respect to temporal sequences in order to mimic realistic conditions of deployment. This strong preprocessing phase paves the way for realistic application of loss formulations Equations 1 - 5 and performance estimations listed in Tables 1, 2 and 3. **3.2 ** **Hybrid Multi-Task Deep Learning Architecture **

The suggested framework applies a multi-task deep learning hybrid model for simultaneously performing fault diagnosis, risk assessment, and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction on NEV systems. First, NEV fault data is loaded and augmented through simulating target variables like fault type, temperature, and vibration to simulate operating conditions in reality; further data augmentation adds to variability. The preprocessed data, with one-hot encoded fault labels for classiﬁcation and continuous values for regression of risk and RUL, is then utilized to train a model that includes a shared backbone for feature extraction, consisting of dense layers with batch normalization and dropout. This common representation is fed to task-speciﬁc heads: a softmax-activated head for fault classiﬁcation, a regression head for risk estimation using a custom physicsinformed loss layer (see Equation 4 ), and a linear regression head for RUL estimation. The total loss function is a weighted sum of categorical cross-entropy Equation 1 and mean squared errors Equations 2 and 3, combined as given in Equation 5, and optimized with Adam optimizer with Early Stopping and learning rate reduction mechanisms. The physics-informed loss function constrains monotonic risk behavior with temperature, whereby predictions meet physical expectations of risk with temperature. This signiﬁcantly enhances model generalization and makes the output interpretable.

**3.3 ** **Uncertainty Estimation with Monte Carlo Dropout **

Considering the safety-critical application of predictive maintenance in EV systems, the model is not only made to generate precise predictions but also give solid estimates Synergistic Fusion of Physics-Informed and Data- Driven Deep

of uncertainty. This is achieved through Monte Carlo Dropout, where several forward passes with dropout on yield a distribution of output predictions. The obtained mean and standard deviation, are quantitative indicators of prediction conﬁdence, especially for RUL estimation, since high overconﬁdence in the predictions might lead to serious misestimations in maintenance planning. Monte Carlo Dropout will make several stochastic forward passes during inference. Then, the distribution of outputs estimates epistemic uncertainty. This is an extremely useful feature in RUL prediction, in which a single incorrect overconﬁdent estimate may lead to unforeseeable maintenance delays. Thus, conﬁdence intervals quantify whether one should trust the model's prediction and facilitate risk-aware decision-making. **3.4 ** **Model Interpretability Using SHAP **

For transparency and interpretability of the model, SHAP is used to explain each prediction by attributing an importance value to each input feature. These SHAP values provide transparent explanations of which sensor measurements are most impactful in every prediction, allowing root-cause analysis when faults are observed or high-risk scores are produced. Visualizations include SHAP plots and waterfall charts that present the contributions of individual features in the three tasks, supplementing the quantitative performance metrics presented in Tables 1, 2 and 3. This interpretability not only empowers trust in the predictions of the model but also enables further model reﬁnement and domain-speciﬁc decision-making. SHAP values enhance the conﬁdence level of the model and help the engineer ﬁnd the key sensor signals. If, for instance, vibration continues to contribute to high-risk scores, technicians will be able to focus their inspection on that particular subsystem. ## 4 **Simulation Results ** **4.1 ** **Experimental Setup **

The available data in this study contains time-series sensor data from EV battery systems with noise injection owing to data augmentation requirements. Each sample contained Voltage (V), Current (A), Motor Speed (RPM), Temperature (°C), Vibration (g), Ambient Temperature (°C), and Humidity (%), correlated to labeled fault types and additional metadata. Standard scaling was applied to bring all sensor features to the same normalized scale. Fault classiﬁcation (with four fault classes), risk score regression (via physics-informed loss layer), and remaining useful life (based on fault type and sensor conditions) were included in the developed multi- task learning framework. The architecture of the model consisted of a shared encoder and task-speciﬁc output heads, early stopping, and learning rate reductions on plateau were adopted during training to avoid overﬁtting and help with convergence.

## 5 **Conclusion **

## In this paper, a strong, interpretable, and physics-constrained deep learning framework

has been presented for electric vehicle fault diagnosis, remaining useful life estimation, and risk prediction. Our domain-speciﬁc physics constraint-enabled multi-task learning approach, along with SHAP-based interpretability, enables physically valid predictions with very high accuracy and low error rates. Including Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation further emphasizes its suitability in safety-critical tasks. Experimental results support the effectiveness of the framework in maximizing predictive maintenance activities. In the future, the model will be extended towards online learning and multisensor fusion to maximize learning adaptability in dynamic situations. Furthermore, the lightweight architecture enables efﬁcient inference on low-power edge devices and thus favors the deployment of real-time inference in NEV systems. This corresponds to onboard, autonomous, and proactive health monitoring without leaning on any cloud infrastructure.

## Adaptive Jitter in Market Simulations **Evaluating Latency Impact Using ABIDES **

Umesh Gupta 1( B ), Samrat Singh Bhandari 1, Sakshi Gupta 2, and Aditya Bhardwaj 1

1 SCSET, Bennett University, Gr. Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201310, India er.umeshgupta@gmail.com, aditya.cse@nitttrchd.ac.in 2 SoCA, MRIIRS University, Faridabad, India

**Abstract. ** In this thesis, we propose to apply an adaptive jitter model to the ABIDES platform as an enhanced latency modeling scheme. Traditional ABIDES latency models (predictable determinism & cubic jitter) neglect market conditions and agent behavior. Network induced delays, as argued, would be better modeled as a dynamic feedback latency model that adjusts to agent behavior and market ﬂow. Our model captures important market features that traditional models overlook, including price dispersion, liquidity droughts, and volatility spillovers. We assess our model by taking a baseline simulation framed within the RMSC03 conﬁguration in the ABIDES simulation suite and comparing it against simulated trading on June 3, 2020, which is characterized by high market activity. ABIDES (AgentBased Interactive Discrete Event Simulation) is a simulation environment that models ﬁnancial markets as a system of interacting autonomous trading agents.. The RMSC03 conﬁguration is one of its standard setups that replicates a realistic limit order book environment. It includes a simulated exchange and a diverse set of agents: a POV (percentage-of-volume) market-making agent, value investors, momentum traders, noise traders, and institutional participants, providing a representative cross-section of market behavior. These improvements make our approach especially suitable for stress testing, high-frequency trading (HFT) analysis, and market stability research, thanks to a tractable and conﬁgurable event-based time model.

**Keywords: ** Market simulation · latency modelling · adaptive jitter · order book dynamics · agent-based modelling · ﬁnancial markets · discrete event simulation · artiﬁcial intelligence

## 1 **Introduction **

(HFT) where microsecond latency changes make the difference in gaining proﬁts \[ 1 \]. Strategies include co location \[ 2 \] and specialized hardware for a network component of arbitrage to minimize consequent delays, but fairness and efﬁciency are thus more sensitive to network induced delays \[ 3 \]. In ABIDES, static or random latencies are used to simulate such environments \[ 4 \]; however, real time dynamics are neglected, compromising agent reliability \[ 5 \]. Cascaded LSTMs with PPO \[ 6 \], RL TD3 based

## 2 **Literature Review **

Recent advances in ﬁnancial market simulations use DRL and multi-agent systems to improve prediction and strategy, but many ignore network latency \[ 1 \]. Zou et al. \[ 5 \] and Sarlakifar et al. \[ 6 \] used LSTM with PPO/TD3 for trading under volatility but omitted real-time delays. Fatemi and Hu \[ 2 \] observed context and memory misalignment in multiple agents- FinVision improved interpretability but communication delays in HFT were left unaddressed. Nguyen et al. \[ 3 \] worked on multi-agent DDPG for edge/blockchain with trust mechanisms and temporal latency was again overlooked. Chi et al. \[ 4 \] used spatiotemporal graphs for volatility modeling and ignored time delays. Yu et al. \[ 12 \]  developed LSTM-ANN and MIGA and similarly lacked an awareness of latency. Almiñana \[ 7 \] examined high-frequency order shifts with Markov chains while presuming instant execution. Fernández et al. \[ 8 \] applied DQNs in ABIDES but there was an assumption of no agent communication. Coletta et al. \[ 11 \] accounted for latency in GAN-based simulations. Delays were also ignored in the studies of Jin \[ 13 \] and Mamillapalli et al. \[ 14 \] which used graphs and sentiment approaches. Our adaptive jitter model addresses this gap by simulating the network-induced delays, improving ABIDES for authentic market modeling. **2.1 ** **Deep Reinforcement Learning for Stock Trading **

The authors greatly advanced stock trading DRL by constructing cascaded LSTM networks alongside Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The research team was able to develop techniques to manage and control volatility, as well as identify patterns in the markets of countries with advanced volatility and unfriendly ﬁnancial conditions. The improvements made to the system allowed better gains during changes in the market. The study found that agents maintained regular communication habits, but no study was made on how delays in the network could affect performance limits. Because these trading delays can signiﬁcantly affect both agent behavior and their returns, this - Gupta et al.

research includes latency adjustments in agent-based models. In 2022, authors Kabbani and Duman \[ 9 \] applied the TD3 algorithm to enhance the trade actions by developing new trading-speciﬁc control systems that function as discrete units. Being fully optimized, the method does not consider the actual usage of network elements that causes signiﬁcant behaviour shifts in agents operating quick trade volumes. The model does not contain active communication features that could lower its performance in situations where rapid communication is necessary. The study introduces a new model that represents both the actual time delays in a network and their impact on operations. **2.2 ** **Multi-Agent Systems and Coordination **

Han et al. \[ 10 \] investigated issues pertaining to memory retention, contextual alignment, and joint decision-making in multi-Agent LLMs. They found that connecting multiple agents at the same time leads to a reduction in available capacity because of memory and context alignment issues. In ﬁnancial simulations, agents interacting with and trading the same instruments under delays of network latency exacerbate these issues and affect trading opportunities in fast-paced markets-especially in the fast-paced instruments of the market. In fast-paced markets, the impact of transmission delays, which relate to the inter-module delays described in Fatemi and Hu \[ 2 \] in the Fin Vision \[ 2 \] system, J, is more pronounced in the text. J is the 12th reference. Without accounting for latency, real-time operations become impractical. The researchers introduced an adaptive jitter model with a time-based mechanism to overcome these simulation limitations \[ 12, 13 \]. **2.3 ** **Microstructure and Agent Interaction Modelling **

The purpose this study how companies under different industry sectors acted and timed their actions in this unusual period. But their research considers the big picture for the market, yet their mathematical approach does not consider actual order processing times because it supposes instant changes. The model lacks a detail that weakens its ability to show what takes place in actual high-frequency trading during fast execution and responses. In 2021, Fernández et al. \[ 13 \] designed a model to guide a market maker by using Deep Q-Learning along with the ABIDES platform in markets with one or more traders. Despite being able to highlight performant trading strategies with reinforcement learning, their work was conﬁned by presuming that the agent could not engage in communication for any length of time. Changes to the tool allow for more accurate market modeling under various network and congestion scenarios which helps improve ﬁnancial simulation research \[ 17 - 21 \].

## 3 **Problem Statement **

- Although ABIDES and other platforms have advanced in their agent-based simulations, existing approaches for modelling latency are still quite simple and don't  accurately reﬂect how communication delays change in ﬁnancial markets. ABIDES framework relies on two simple latency models, deterministic latency and cubic jitter, for performing simulations \[ 12 - 14 \].

Adaptive Jitter in Market Simulations: Evaluating Latency Impact

- **Deterministic latency ** assumes ﬁxed delay times that depends on agent geographical  positions generates consistent uniform communication delays. - **Cubic jitter ** adds unexpected changes in latency by using a heavy-tails distribution.  The dynamics of both market changes and agent actions which inﬂuence network delays, are not accounted for by the variability added in the model \[ 15, 16 \].

These static models operate without any time-based or behaviour-responsive feedback structures which would let latency develop chronologically. The models fail to include variables that result from rising agent message activity or market exchange congestion together with agent response strategies during market trading periods or news events. The problems with existing latency modelling approaches generate three signiﬁcant issues.

1. **Underestimation of Systemic Risk: ** When agents all act the same due to high risks or  market turmoil, the lack of dynamic latency can result in a lack of important feedback. This may hide important weaknesses in the way market's function, making it hard to discover problems created by latency. Multiple companies reacting to the same lag often increases the chances of systemic risk, causing rapid and repeated problems \[ 17, 19 \]. 2. **Overestimation of Strategy Robustness: ** Advance modeling for strategies leads to  the false belief that certain trading strategies such as those used by arbitrage bots, smart order routers and market makers, are robust to unpredictable network problems. They depend on rapid ways to communicate to decide what to buy or sell and carry out trades. Because they do not consider how delays in networks may affect results, existing models often present inaccurately positive outcomes, without considering the major problems caused by latency in high-frequency trading \[ 19, 21 \]. 3. **Inaccurate Modelling of Market Phenomena: ** Often, basic latency models do not  fully explain how spread widening, order book thinning and price slippage happen. They are caused by both changing core values and by short, sudden pauses and overloading within existing networks. Existing models have difﬁculty matching actual events in the market, leading to poor results during high-frequency trading. They reduce the value of ABIDES for handling stress testing, analyzing AI strategies and doing research on the stability of markets in changing conditions \[ 18, 20 \].

Using advanced, time-sensitive latency models greatly improves these simulations and helps us learn more about how delays due to networks impact the functioning of ﬁnancial markets. This work explains a jitter model that improves itself with each new condition, overcoming those issues and capturing the impact of latency on markets and performance of trading agents \[ 14 - 16 \].

## 4 **Methodology **

In this study, we aimed to systematically evaluate the inﬂuence of different latency modelling approaches on agent-based market behavior. To achieve this, we conducted an in-depth comparative study using the ABIDES (Agent-Based Interactive Discrete Event Simulation) platform. ABIDES is a highly modular and extensible simulation environment that is widely used for market microstructure research. - Gupta et al.

Figure 4 shows workﬂow of the simulation study on ABIDES platform for evaluating latency models in ﬁnancial markets. The different steps are: First, deﬁning the objective of the study and then conﬁguring the RMSC03 market setup in ABIDES. The several deployed agents include the exchange, market maker, value, momentum, noise, and execution agents. Further, several latency models are implemented such as deterministic latency, cubic jitter latency, and the adaptive jitter model proposed here **. ** Simulations are run for a speciﬁc timeframe (June 3, 2020, from 09:30 AM to 11:30 AM), after which results such as price, liquidity, and volume are collected and compared. The last step includes assessing the effectiveness of the adaptive jitter model compared to the other options. The market conﬁguration employed operated on the widely recognized and frequently utilized RMSC03 reference setup. This arrangement was designed to support different types of agents, each showcasing the diverse strategies and behaviors observed in actual markets. In particular, the conﬁguration included these components:

**• Exchange Agent: ** One exchange agent assumed the responsibility of simulating the limit order book. The agent-maintained market steadiness by consolidating purchase and trade guidelines and dispatched estimates and transaction information to all other agents. Market interactions all took place through the exchange agent, who also ensured that trades followed the current market trends.

- **POV Market Maker Agent**: We also inserted a market maker agent for POV (Participation of Volume) to act as a provider of liquidity. This agent purchased and sold  in line with the whole market's trading volume to keep the market liquid and wellfunctioning. The market maker behaved according to set guidelines that imitated real liquidity strategies. - **Value Agents**: Many value agents were designed to model real investors who trade  when the differences between prices and their internal models are signiﬁcant. As designed, these agents modeled real-world techniques that evaluate future prices to make investment plans, not brief changes in the stock market. - **Momentum Agents**: Our model had 25 momentum agents to show how trendfollowing works. Such agents handle programs that sense new price changes and  respond immediately. These agents imitated trend-following approaches, enabling the market to change rapidly and mirror the trading actions of those who beneﬁt from fast variations in price. - **Noise Agents**: We simulated the placement by introducing a large group of 5,000  noise agents for random scenarios. They strengthened the market by adding depth and kept it exciting, so traders had a more lifelike experience. The presence of these noise agents made the market more uncertain, allowing sudden trades to affect prices and market liquidity. - **POV Execution Agent**: An agent representing institutional strategies was available  as an alternative POV in all the scenarios and was included when selected. According to the rules given, this agent traded a speciﬁc amount within given time intervals or at VWAP. The addition of this agent increased realism because it modeled the operating style of large groups of ﬁnancial traders.

Using a ﬁxed random seed (42) and focusing on June 3, 2020, a day with high liquidity and trading activity, the study analyzed the market on the 09:30 to 11:30 AM time block which is a period of intensive trading. By keeping all other factors constant

Adaptive Jitter in Market Simulations: Evaluating Latency Impact **Fig. 4 ** workﬂow diagram

apart from the latency model, the different types of latencies on the model and their impact on the price, liquidity, and volume of trade were measured. This demonstrated that the adaptive jitter model performs well in all market conditions. **4.1 ** **Latency Models **

Three different delay patterns for communication were examined in the simulation, providing unique ways to model how long it takes for agents to communicate in the ABIDES simulation environment.

1. **Deterministic Latency**: A consistent time gap is determined for agents based only on  where each is located. As long as the environment is not disrupted, the latency doesn't change. Removing variability gives the model a standard scenario for researchers to - Gupta et al.

study the effects of other variables on the market's actions. How stable it is makes it appropriate for planned experiments. 2. **Cubic Jitter**: Unlike in the deterministic case, the cubic jitter model also includes  random latency because it uses a heavy-tailed cubic distribution. In general, latency is calculated by using a random variable, latency = min \_latency + *a * *x* 3 \times min \_latency jitter\_unit

a: jitter strength x ∼ U(jitter\_clip,1\] (random variable drawn from uniform distribu tion). min\_latency and jitter\_unit are simulation parameters.

The jitter coefﬁcient a can be set at any value using conﬁguration. This approach reﬂects unpredictable latencies, similar to those in actual highfrequency trading, where network problems tend to appear randomly. It adds realism because latency can change and pattern over the course of the attack. 3. **Adaptive Jitter (Proposed): ** latency = min \_latency + a · \sigma(t) *x* 3 \times min \_latency jitter\_unit

In the adaptive jitter case only, there is the introduction of a sigmoid scaling factor, σ (t). Improved adjustments of the ABIDES latency framework allows this new model to perform changes in latency during communication or time adjustments. For this model, the calculation of jitter is separated into four segments, and it employs an evolving sigmoid scaling function, where time or message volume changes the range of the sigmoid scaling function. This model accommodates an increase in average response time gradually, which is a consequence of greater network trafﬁc. It demonstrates appropriate and improved changes to the latency as the system load rises. This is done by subclassing Latency Model in ABIDES and incorporating an adaptive\_jitter mode, which provides the researchers the ability to simulate adaptable and meaningful latency patterns. The main objective of the latency models was to determine the impact of different delay types on market actions. The adaptive jitter model is especially valuable to those who control the system because it mirrors the network and delay changes in actual systems, thus streamlining access for additional handlers to the system.

However, the various latency types were deterministic, cubic jitter, and adaptive jitter. The agents were set, market time was the same, and to ensure fairness in analyses, each experiment used a ﬁxed random seed. We were interested in examining the differences, if any, in market types in terms of the price stability, spread behavior, book liquidity, and volume of trade.

## 6 **Conclusion **

Incorporating the adaptive jitter within ABIDES, the realism of simulated network delays has increased, along with the capture of current market trading behaviour. Unlike ﬁxed, cubic, or other jitter types leveraging sigmoid functions where connectedness is ignored, ABIDES adaptive jitter considers network interactions and the system's stress response. ABIDES adaptive jitter's inter-temporal consideration of bid-ask spreads, wash trading, and trading volume improves the accuracy of simulated network delayed paths. These advancements provide ABIDES with improved realism for training AI systems and for benchmarking AI systems designed for market research, compliance-linked stress testing, dynamic trading algorithm development, and adaptive trading strategy formulation. Unlike ﬁxed models that simulate jitter as an unbalanced network stress, the adaptive approach models system latency more accurately. Future development possibilities on the adaptive model's predictive potential and utility are extensive. Examples of substantial work include real-time latency model calibration, the exploration of learning agents, and inter-exchange latency impact analysis. Optimizing ABIDES for distributed

Adaptive Jitter in Market Simulations: Evaluating Latency Impact

## use is a prerequisite for predictive accuracy as well as conducting large-scale, frequent

simulations. Testing the system with regulator-mandated market rules enables crisis testing, while DDoS simulations reveal model stress points. Using both live and simulation information together helps with fast strategy review and anticipating dangers in the future.

## Joint QoS-aware Energy and Spectrum Efﬁcient

**Scheduling in NGMN HetNet Downlink Using ** **Carrier Aggregation **

## Yong-Chun Kim, Chol Jong ( B ), Chol-Ryong Song, and Hui-Song Ri

High-Tech Research and Development Center, Kim Il Sung University, Pyongyang, Democratic People's Republic of Korea c.jong1104@ryongnamsan.edu.kp

**Abstract. ** The interference situation is complicated in NGMN (Next Generation Mobile Networks) Heterogeneous Network (HetNet) with ultra-dense femtocells and many different types of users, and the resource allocation mechanism is also diversiﬁed. Previous approaches have dealt separately with energy and spectrum efﬁciency issues, resource allocation issues to improve QoS by reducing packet loss rates, and some studies to combine different approaches, such as tradeoff of power saving schemes and spectrum efﬁciency enhancement schemes, have been reported, but there has not yet been an introduction to resource allocation schemes to trade-off energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency with respect to the service ﬂow pattern. Specially, there is no report on the combination of energy efﬁciency optimization and real-time resource allocation in NGMN downlink. We ﬁrst propose to choose an appropriate resource allocation scheme, whether to improve energy efﬁciency or to improve spectral efﬁciency, based on network state information such as channel condition or load state in situations where resources are insufﬁcient to be allocated to all active users. Next, we propose an optimization scheme to improve energy efﬁciency in NGMN downlink with carrier aggregation, and, we propose a new algorithm to combinate this optimization scheme with the real-time resource allocation scheme. Based on this, a new metric considering energy efﬁciency and QoS service type is proposed. The proposed resource allocation method is validated through simulation experiments. Simulation results show that the proposed method not only provides a tradeoff between spectral efﬁciency and energy efﬁciency, but also reduces the packet loss rate and ensures QoS.

**Keywords: ** spectrum efﬁciency · heterogeneous network · energy efﬁciency

## 1 **Introduction **

## In \[ 1, 2 \], an overview of resource allocation methods for maximizing trafﬁc, resource

allocation methods for ensuring fairness, and Exponential Proportional Fair (EXP/PF) methods considering packet loss rates and fairness is presented and a combination of them is proposed. In \[ 3 - 5 \], authors proposed a method to adapt a reasonable resource allocation algorithm according to the service type. In the LTE/LTE-A network, a resource

© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026 - Virdee et al. (Eds.): ICAIN 2025, LNNS 1931, pp. 27-51, 2026.  <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-23314-1\_3> Y.-C. Kim et al.

allocation approach \[ 6 \] to achieve two or more goals simultaneously by combining different objective functions, or a resource allocation approach \[ 7 \] to achieve a tradeoff between mutually exclusive objective functions is also proposed. These methods have proposed new metric and have attempted to achieve or tradeoff two or more objectives simultaneously by introducing different objective factors into them \[ 8, 9 \]. The resource allocation problem in LTE-A/5G networks using carrier aggregation is complex compared to that in LTE networks. This is because in the LTE-A/5G network, there exist several component carriers (CC) and the resource blocks corresponding to each component carrier have to be allocated reasonably for certain purposes \[ 10 - 12 \].

In \[ 13 \], a study on energy efﬁcient resource allocation in HetNet using NOMA technology is presented. In \[ 14 \], the authors propose a resource allocation scheme to speed up the data transmission rate of users at the edge of a small cell in a CoMP-Enabled NOMA network. XIAOYI ZHANG, XIAORONG ZHU, AND HONGBO ZHU \[24\] proposed an algorithm to partition users into a number of clusters that allow all users in a single cluster to share a beamforming vector in a MIMO-NOMA network and further reduce inter-cluster interference, based on which a method to optimally allocate channels and power is proposed. In addition, efforts to optimize energy efﬁciency and reduce power consumption have been introduced in NOMA systems, which are regarded as 5G connection technologies \[ 15 \]. In LTE-A/5G networks, optimization methods such as nonlinear programming, artiﬁcial intelligence techniques such as deep neural networks and genetic algorithms, and different mathematical methods are being explored for resource allocation. We have already reported a study on resource allocation in 5G networks using NOMA using deep neural networks \[ 16 \] and also proposed a method to solve NP-Hard optimization problem. The disadvantage of these energy efﬁciency optimization methods is that they are computationally expensive, and a lot of time and labor is consumed in the preprocessing. Therefore, these methods are unsuitable for practical use in providing real-time scheduling with 1 ms update period. In addition, the results show that resource allocation schemes using a single objective function are not able to respond to modern mobile networks that require a variety of service types and simultaneously satisfying the objectives of different indicators, and that a rational combination of different methods is more effective. Hence, we ﬁrst propose a novel resource allocation method to achieve a tradeoff between energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency while simultaneously reducing packet loss rate. In this paper, we ﬁrst propose a mechanism to properly choose between scheduling methods for energy efﬁciency and scheduling methods for spectrum efﬁciency according to the channel state. Considering the network conditions such as channel condition or network load, choosing an appropriate schedule is a guarantee to achieve a tradeoff between energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency.

Next, we propose an optimization method to maximize energy efﬁciency, and the disadvantage of this method is that it is difﬁcult to achieve real-time performance due to the large number of users with high computational cost. To overcome this shortcoming, a new mechanism is proposed to combine the optimization method with an average energy efﬁciency improvement scheme. As a result, the energy efﬁciency value updated in real time will have a value close to the optimal value and will be entered into the energy efﬁciency fairness metric to determine the priority of resource allocation.

Joint QoS-aware Energy and Spectrum Efﬁcient Scheduling in NGMN

An energy efﬁcient fairness metric is also proposed in this paper. The energy efﬁciency fairness metric also considers the delay of HOL (Head of Line) packets according to the service ﬂow type. In addition, we also propose a new metric that considers spectral efﬁciency and service type, and accordingly determine the resource allocation priority of UEs. Through simulation, the proposed resource allocation method is compared and analyzed with previous resource allocation methods and its usefulness is veriﬁed.

The main contributions of this paper are as follows. First, in LTE-A/5G HetNet using carrier aggregation technique, we formulate a set of equations to optimize energy efﬁciency by considering the inter-cell interference and propose a new transformation and algorithm to solve the NP-Hard problem.

Secondly, we propose a new metric considering energy efﬁciency and QCI and a new metric considering spectral efﬁciency and QCI, based on which we propose a resource allocation method to determine resource allocation priority.

Third, we classiﬁed UEs into clusters to improve energy efﬁciency and that to improve spectral efﬁciency, and applied energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency enhancement schemes separately to each cluster to enhance the effectiveness of each scenario.

Fourth, a scheduling algorithm considering the time taken to solve the optimization problem is proposed and the effectiveness of the proposed methods is veriﬁed through simulation.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 summarizes related works. Section 3 describes the system model and our proposed resource allocation framework. In Sect. 4, we present an optimization method for energy efﬁciency enhancement in LTEA/5G HetNet downlink and an algorithm for solving it, combining this method with a real-time resource allocation method, and a new metric combining energy efﬁciency and QoS requirements. Thus, in Sect. 4, methods to meet the QoS requirements and improve energy efﬁciency are presented. In Sect. 5, a method for enhancing spectral efﬁciency and QoS on LTE-A/5G downlink is proposed. We also propose a new metric, based on which the priority of resource allocation is determined. In Sect. 6, simulation and comparison results with previous methods are provided. In Chap. 7, we conclude the paper.

## 2 **Related Works **

Research on improving energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency in LTE-A/5G HetNet has been continued in recent years.

In \[ 17 \], a resource allocation approach for energy efﬁciency enhancement in heterogeneous cellular networks powered by renewable energy sources is investigated. In order to maximize the energy efﬁciency of the network, overcome the power supply instability of renewable energy sources, and ensure the fairness of users, the authors deﬁne the energy efﬁciency with the sum weight of all links in HetNet as the objective function. In this work, power is allocated using a water-ﬁlling scheme, and a low complexity distributed resource allocation method using reinforcement learning is proposed. In \[ 18 \], a resource allocation method for optimizing energy efﬁciency in uplink-downlink decoupled 5G HetNet was studied, transforming the convex fractional programming problem Y.-C. Kim et al.

into a convex optimization problem using the CCT (Charnes-Cooper Transformation). The transformed problem was solved using an approximation algorithm. Handan Zheng et al. \[ 19 \] formulated a fractional programming problem that allocates resource blocks and power under constraints that limit the capacity of the backhaul link in 5G HetNet and converted this nonconvex optimization problem into a convex-concave subprogramming problem to solve the convex optimization theory. Speciﬁcally, the authors propose a method of combining resource block and power allocation for users in each cell under different backhaul capacity constraints. In \[ 20 \], resource allocation schemes have been proposed to optimize the throughput of the system in small cells using CA while ensuring the energy efﬁciency and system stability of the network. The authors adopted an iterative optimal MCS-based search algorithm to solve the high-order NPHard assignment problem. In \[ 21 \], an efﬁcient fractional-frequency reuse-based spectral partitioning scheme is proposed to reduce inter-tier interference in order to optimally manage energy consumption and interference in 5G HetNet, where the femtocell and D2D communications coexist with macro cells, and different optimization problems for resource allocation in different tiers are proposed.

However, the following issues are poorly studied. First, in NGMN (Next Generation Mobile Networks)(LTE-A/NR(Next Radio)) HetNet using carrier aggregation, joint resource block and power allocation optimization schemes to trade-off spectral efﬁciency and energy efﬁciency in UEs with different channel conditions are less studied.

Second, there is little mention of providing user fairness and QoS requirements as much as possible in resource allocation for energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency.

Third, there is little research on the problem of solving the optimization problem in real time. The problem of improving the accuracy of the optimization problem has been extensively addressed, but the computational time and the application of it to the real environment have not been studied much.

To solve the above problems, we have proposed more enhanced resource allocation schemes.

## 3 **System Model **

In this section, we present a system model and mathematical model for QoS-aware scheduling while tradeoff between energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency in NGMN (Next Generation Mobile Networks) downlink, and provide a framework for resource allocation. **3.1 ** **Scheduling Architecture in NGMN HetNet **

Figure 1 illustrates the resource allocation mechanism in NGMN downlink. The NGMN consists of a core network consisting of AMF (Access and Mobility Management Function), SMF (Session Management Function), UPF (User Plane Function), and a cell consisting of gNB and UE. At the MAC layer of gNB, resource allocation to UEs with different kinds of services is performed, while the probability of packet loss increases as the buffer delay of the MAC layer increases. When we consider packet loss due to

**3.2 ** **The Proposed Framework for Resource Allocation in the Work **

Figure 2 shows our resource allocation framework in the article.

As shown in Fig. 2, we choose the resource allocation scheme using the metric for resource allocation scheme selection. It is then decided whether to use an energyefﬁcient or a spectrum-efﬁcient scheme. Then, in each energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency scenario, the resource allocation priority of UEs is determined and resources are allocated accordingly, using the metric considering QoS, respectively. **3.3 ** **Selection of Scheduling Schemes **

We ﬁrst propose a selection of scheduling methods. We chose the channel quality indicator (CQI) as a criterion to modify the scheduling policy in downlink.

Joint QoS-aware Energy and Spectrum Efﬁcient Scheduling in NGMN

## 4

**Scheduling to Improve Energy Efﬁciency in NGMN HetNet ** **Downlink **

First, based on a new mathematical formulation of the scheduling method to optimize EE for NGMN downlink with carrier aggregation, an algorithm is proposed to solve it. Next, an algorithm is proposed to combine the optimal EE by optimization method and the average EE by difference equation in order to ensure the real-time performance of the scheduler that must be updated over a period of 1 ms. Finally, a new metric is presented to meet the QoS requirements and improve energy efﬁciency.

The equation set ( 15-1 ), ( 15-2 ), ( 15\_a )~( 15\_f ) is a linear-least square problem and can be transformed into quadratic programming \[45\]. Table 1 gives the algorithm for solving the set of equations ( 26 ). Using this algorithm, power and bandwidth optimized for energy efﬁciency in NGMN microcell downlink are assigned to UEs. At this time, the interference of the femtocell is taken into account. The interference given by the femtocell can be estimated based on the resource allocation information in the femtocell. The resource allocation information in the femtocell is given as an initial condition.

Table 2 gives the algorithm to obtain the global power and bandwidth allocation. Once the solution is obtained, we can also calculate the energy efﬁciency value *e* *k*, *n * of each UE on the *n* th CC in downlink using Eq. ( 1 ). The energy efﬁciency, power and bandwidth calculated will be the criteria of resource allocation as a result of solving the optimal equation. Therefore, updating energy efﬁciency based on this value and determining resource allocation priority based on it will be able to achieve high energy efﬁciency in downlink by more approaching energy efﬁciency to the optimal value and assigning high resource allocation priority to the UE with high energy efﬁciency. **4.1.3 ** **Update Energy Efﬁciency Considering Historic **

The frequency band available in the NGMN downlink is up to 20 MHz/400 MHz, and the bandwidth can be extended to 100 MHz/6.4 GHz due to the availability of up to 5/16 CCs using the carrier aggregation technique at NGMN. The frequency space of the Y.-C. Kim et al.

subcarriers in each CC is 15 kHz × 2 *n * ( *n* ∈ \{1,2,3\}), and the number of subcarriers varies depending on the numerology. The modulation and coding rates for each subcarrier can be different. Different MCS (Modulation and Coding Scheme) might be applied to every subcarrier. However, the MCS value assigned to one UE during a single TTI cycle is considered the same. The value of the MCS applied here is determined according to the current channel conditions of the UE. In the time domain, a frame is 10 ms and consists of 10 subframes. One subframe consists of two time slots (0.5 ms) and one time slot consists of six to seven symbols depending on the length of the cyclic preﬁx (CP).

As a result, we can consider the performance change of the proposed method with varying threshold, varying χ value (i.e., changing the amount of resource blocks applying the spectral efﬁciency scheme, or changing the a mount of resource blocks applying the energy efﬁciency enhancement scheme). As shown in Fig. 4, the spectral efﬁciency of the proposed method is large compared to other methods. This effect is striking as the number of UEs increases, it is due to allocating resources to increase the spectral efﬁciency when resources are insufﬁcient. Among the proposed methods, the scenario according to Case 2 have high spectral efﬁciency, because the spectral efﬁciency mode is applied even for those with slightly low channel state when threshold is low.by doing so, the spectral efﬁciency will increase as the spectral efﬁciency mode application targets increase. Also, a large χ value cause increasing the number of resource blocks allocated to UEs where the spectrum efﬁciency scheme is applied. This will result in some improvement of the spectral efﬁciency. The lower performance of the GA and JRAUAPC methods in terms of spectral efﬁciency is due to decreasing efﬁciency of the corresponding methods due to channel condition variations when the number of users i ncreases.

Figure 4 shows the performance comparison from the energy efﬁciency point of view. As can be seen, the proposed methods are superior to the traditional EXP/PF, MLDF, PF, etc. in terms of energy efﬁciency. However, the GA scheme and JRAUAPC method are slightly higher (in Cases 3 and 4). It means that in this case, the proposed method

Overall, the proposed method is slightly superior and not inferior to the recently proposed methods in terms of energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency, which are due to further improving the efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency by classifying UEs according to channel conditions and applying a suitable scheduling scheme for each class. Next, the proposed method signiﬁcantly improves the performance in QoS index such as packet loss rate, which is due to the introduction of a metric function considering packet loss rate in scheduling. As a result, the data ﬂow is also greatly improved. The introduction of metric functions to ensure fairness in resource allocation also improves user fairness. In conclusion, the simulation results show that the proposed scheme is superior to the previous one in several aspects.

## 7 **Conclusion **

In this paper, we proposed various schemes and efﬁcient metric and algorithms to improve energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency while considering QoS in NGMN(LTEA/NR) HetNet downlink. We determined whether an energy efﬁcient scheme is applied, or a spectrum efﬁciency scheme is applied considering the channel condition between UE and gNB, and then applied a suitable scheduling scheme. This increased the effectiveness of energy efﬁciency and spectrum efﬁciency enhancement schemes. In addition, we

Joint QoS-aware Energy and Spectrum Efﬁcient Scheduling in NGMN

proposed a new metric to prioritize resource allocation in energy efﬁciency and spectral efﬁciency schemes, respectively. First, in the energy efﬁciency scheme, a new combined algorithm was proposed to combine the energy efﬁciency value obtained by the average energy efﬁciency update expression with the optimized energy efﬁciency value and the historical one obtained by the energy efﬁciency optimal resource allocation method. By doing so, a new approach to apply energy efﬁcient optimization method to realtime scheduling is proposed. In the energy efﬁcient optimal resource allocation method, we mathematically formulated the system of energy efﬁcient optimization equations in NGMN HetNet downlink and proposed new algorithm to solve the NP-Hard problem. In addition, the effect of the optimization solution computation time on the performance of the combined algorithm was evaluated through simulations, and it was concluded that the proposed combined algorithm can be applied better to objects with low mobility and low number of users. Next, we proposed a more advanced metric function to ensure QoS and energy efﬁciency proportional fairness (EXP/EEPF) in energy efﬁciency (EE) scheme and QoS and spectral efﬁciency fairness (EXP/SEPF) in the spectral efﬁciency (SE) scheme. The results of the simulation showed that the proposed scheme achieves signiﬁcant performance improvement compared to other previous schemes in terms of energy efﬁciency, spectral efﬁciency and fairness. This performance improvement was accompanied by an improvement in the trafﬁc performance. However, in this paper, we are still limited to the study of OFDMA-based NGMN, and we will extend our work to resource allocation problem in NOMA in the future. Thus, our method showed superior performance in several aspects compared to the traditional previous methods.

## Advancing Urban Security: A Random Forest **Approach to Predictive Crime Analytics **

Manas Sisodia 1, Isha Mehra 1, Keerti Shrivastava 2, Neha Dhiman 3, and Monica Bhutani 1( B )

1 Bharati Vidyapeeth's College of Engineering, New Delhi, India monica.bhutani@bharatividyapeeth.edu

2 ITM University, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India kirti.shrivastava.mca@itmuniversity.ac.in 3 Department of Computer Science and Engineering Chandigarh Group of Colleges Jhanjeri, Mohali 140307, Punjab, India

**Abstract. ** This work outlines the creation of a full-scale IoT anti-theft motorcycle system which implements biometric security measures to boost protection standards. Traditional locking mechanisms fail to safeguard motorcycles adequately because motorcycle theft cases continue to rise. The system combines a ﬁngerprint SENSOR and NodeMCU MICROCONTROLLER which enables authorized access for starting the vehicle. The system uses GPS module with GSM communication to transmit real-time motorcycle location after it detects an unauthorized access attempt which then automatically activates alerts. The system incorporates an emergency alert solution which improves general safety measures. This system supports an Android application to allow remote control functions and status overview while tracking devices in real-time. The system presents three main characteristics of affordable equipment combined with user-friendly functionality and dependable operation to promote broad adoption. The system has conﬁrmed its performance as an antitheft solution through experimental examinations that demonstrated its capabilities for theft defense and instant response. The proposed security model unites biometric authentication with IoT systems while resolving standing two-wheeler system vulnerabilities to create an implementation framework for different use scenarios.

**Keywords: ** Invest · assets · ﬁnancial market · abnormality · predict · accuracy · machine learning · model · human intelligence · scientiﬁc research · algorithm · crime prediction · complex task

## 1 **Introduction **

## The escalating number of motorcycle thefts throughout urban regions and rural areas gen

erates major concerns among security forces and private individuals. Motorcycles rank high among stolen vehicles because they possess three critical characteristics including their manageable size alongside affordability and user-friendly operation. Basic anti-theft items consisting of mechanical locks and chain locks together with ignition

Advancing Urban Security: A Random Forest Approach to Predictive

keys offer weak security which basic intruders can easily overcome. Stolen motorcycles remain unrecoverable because modern monitoring systems and real-time alert capabilities are not currently implemented thus creating losses and safety issues along with inconvenience for victims. A self-made intelligent security solution designed exclusively for motorcycles needs to be established to tackle this issue effectively.

The Internet of Things (IoT) together with wireless communication technologies and biometric security systems has produced opportunities to construct advanced vehicle protection systems. IoT makes possible time-sensitive data exchange while enabling remote control functions and automation by interconnecting physical devices to internet infrastructure. Motorcycle security systems gain surveillance continuity and geo-tracking functionality through the deployment of these system features. Parallel to this development ﬁngerprint recognition through biometric authentication provides extremely reliable and personalized access authentication. Access control through biometric credentials blocks unauthorized entry because these credentials possess distinct authenticity which makes them nearly impossible to counterfeit.

**Fig. 1 ** System architecture of the proposed IoT-based motorcycle anti-theft and safety system, illustrating the integration of biometric authentication, GPS tracking, GSM communication, and mobile application interface

The research develops an IoT-based motorcycle security solution which adds ﬁngerprint biometric checks to enable better vehicle access control. The system uses NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller to handle sensors while coordinating module interactions. Motorcycle ignition gets activated only after the ﬁngerprint sensor recognizes the user's identity. When an unauthorized ﬁngerprint matches the system the alarm activates and it sends real-time GPS tracking information to the device of the motorcycle owner through GSM communication. Figure 1 displays the system architecture through a block diagram that shows how hardware modules link with the cloud/mobile interface.

Besides anti-theft protection the system proposes adding automatic accident detection followed by emergency alert functionality. The system automatically triggers an - Sisodia et al.

emergency message which contains GPS position information and sends it to the previously registered emergency contact contacts. The system combines an Android application which lets users check vehicle location through real-time tracking and provides remote access to monitoring alerts. The system beneﬁts from improved usability and enhanced security as well as easier access which leads to better system convenience.

The unique feature of this study stands out due to its simultaneous integration of efﬁcient pricing with biometric controls and immediate tracking while offering accident help functions. The current system landscape features products that prioritize either security from theft or demonstrate several features with missing biometric authentication. Commercially available devices either remain inaccessible due to expensive costs alongside technical installation needs which restrict usage for general users in developing areas. The main original contributions of this research include:

- A ﬁngerprint recognition system functions as the main authentication method to  authorize motorcycle start-ups which blocks unauthorized users from operating the motorcycle due to key loss or duplicate issues. - GPS and GSM modules create a system that enables real-time tracking and immediate  alerts when theft attempts occur which helps owners recover their stolen vehicles. - The system comprises a warning system comprising automated accident detection which transmits emergency notices with geographic coordinates to subscribed  individuals to improve safety for riders. - The system architecture features inexpensive widespread components so it becomes  practical for wide implementation across various settings with limited resources.

Section 2 of this publication contains a review of available documents which demonstrates weaknesses in motorcycle protection systems presently in use. Section 3 details the system architecture, hardware components, and design methodology. The fourth section discusses the software implementation which covers both ﬁrmware integration with the Android mobile application. The section contains experimental ﬁndings and a performance evaluation system based on real-world tests. The paper concludes with future improvement directions in Sect. 6.

## 2 **Literature Review **

Crime analysis and crime prediction have undergone tremendous evolution over the last decade, driven by rapid advancements in data analytics and machine learning systems. The previous approaches to crime forecasting usually relied on classical statistical techniques, such as linear regression, time series prediction, and hot spot mapping. Simple crime prediction methods yielded good initial results, but they had numerous shortcomings, as they demonstrated poor performance in recognizing complex patterns. Additionally, they required non-mobile data to be in a stationary state, which prevented them from processing information in real-time. Machine learning came up to address these issues by coming up with powerful and adaptive advanced models that are data intensive and extract the ﬁner details of association between data in crime databases.

Wang et al. \[ 1 \] created among the ﬁrst crime hot-spot detection systems through their application of logistic regression. The model utilized past criminal records to create

Advancing Urban Security: A Random Forest Approach to Predictive

readable binary results showing whether particular areas would have criminal events. Logistic regression demonstrated weaknesses when analyzing multiple distorted patterns in urban settings which resulted in poor performance for complex prediction tasks. The model demonstrated great transparency but its basic design structure limited its potential to classify crimes at different levels of complexity.

Mohler et al. \[ 2 \] developed spatio-temporal point process models that extended spatial awareness in crime forecasting to monitor both time-based distributions and geographical patterns of crime events. This method analyzed crimes as random occurrences while creating an equation that explained their frequency based on their past distribution for continuously evaluating risk across urban areas. With its proven success in populated urban territories the method became difﬁcult to implement due to computational strains and difﬁculties related to continuous event stream analytics and the processing of detailed geospatial data records. The model produced lower-to-average detection results in zones where data collection was scarce or crime reports were irregular.

The authors Ahmed et al. \[ 3 \] employed decision trees and random forests to perform crime classiﬁcation through integration of temporal and geographical features because structured and semi-structured data needed specialized models. The ensemble approaches produced more accurate results than regression techniques because they effectively addressed non-linear relationships and complex feature relationships. The ability of random forests to overﬁt data reaches a peak when operated improperly on noisy or imbalanced datasets. Despite their weaknesses in accuracy forecasting random forests became common in police departments because of their interpretability and robust characteristics.

Support Vector Machines (SVMs) functioned well as a predictive tool for criminal activity especially when crime classes were easy to differentiate from one another. The research team led by Cheng et al. \[ 4 \] used SVMs to detect crime categories and foresee repeated offenses successfully handling datasets of reasonable sizes. The increase in data complexity along with its larger size rendered SVMs increasingly restricted in terms of scaling performance as well as requiring meticulous parameter adjustments. Because SVMs use kernel-based processing they struggled to meet the requirements of real-time and large-scale deployment for smart policing systems.

Bharathi and Rajalakshmi \[ 5 \] implemented k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) algorithms to classify crime events through historical comparison of similar cases which provided both effective results and easy interpretation with short training requirements. Processing power consumed signiﬁcantly during prediction because k-NN required high computational resources for dealing with big datasets that included many features. The method demonstrated limited reliability because it failed to maintain stability when dealing with irregular or corrupted crime data patterns.

Ensemble learning techniques gained increasing popularity because they helped overcome individual model limitations. The research of Kumar et al. \[ 6 \] tested the potential of joining Random Forests with Gradient Boosting Machines (GBMs) into a single model framework. Research showed ensemble models perform better than single models especially in predictive tasks where crime data varies between geographic locations and timeframes. Such models worked best when combined with extensive hyperparameter optimization and access to robust computational infrastructure. - Sisodia et al.

Deep learning gave a breakthrough to crime forecasting since the method enabled the models to learn useful representations of raw data. In their study, Singh et al. \[ 7 \] have used Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in the analysis of crime trends. The information pertaining to temporal crimes was passed through the LSTM networks that incorporated gated units with memory cells to track long-term dependencies to achieve the best predictive outcomes. It required huge quantities of labeled information and sophisticated computers to work efﬁciently in the instance of training. Such systems lacked transparency, which created issues of interpretability as well as the accountability to the public safety in case these systems are used to predict crime.

The increased interest in XAI was due to these concerns. Similar ﬁndings were reﬂected in the study by Patel and Sharma \[ 8 \] who showed that trust and transparency would be enhanced by incorporating interpretability techniques in crime predictive systems. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Modelagnostic Explanations) were model-agnostic algorithms used by the researchers on existing classiﬁers to ensure the law enforcement personnel and policymakers comprehended the reasons behind model decisions. These methods were successful when implemented but they had to make tradeoffs between accuracy rates and computational needs.

The mixture of the research reveals the development of crime forecasting beyond the rudimentary rule-based mechanisms into sophisticated learning-based methods. The overall concept that runs through all the works suggests that model makers need to choose between improved predictions, rapid processing, and simpler representations of ﬁndings. LSTMs and other deep learning models perform better on large datasets than traditional models, but Random Forests and logistic regression have more validity due to their ability to provide understandable results with fewer processing needs.

The contemporary literature in Table 1 identiﬁes three key points that involve the use of data driven model selection methods and mindful feature development processes, as well as ethical data management practices. Introduction of machine learning into crime prevention demands complete impartiality accompanied by prejudice avoidance and complete responsibility in delicate areas. Multidimensional systems that integrate machine learning with domain knowledge, geospatial analytics, and user-friendly interfaces will be of great importance in the development of crime prevention infrastructure for smart cities.

Various theoretical models have been applied to the crime prediction area including the rule-based frameworks through to the hybrid frameworks. The representative studies can be found in Table 1 as they describe their particular limitations. Early rule-based systems were found to have problems in dealing with shifting urban criminal patterns \[ 8 \]. The logistic regression models \[ 9 \] and decision trees \[ 10 \] yielded better results, but they were not without problems, due to issues with overﬁtting and class imbalance. More sophisticated machines, such as the Support Vector Machines \[ 11 \], k-Nearest Neighbors \[ 12 \], and Artiﬁcial Neural Networks \[ 13 \], demanded a large amount of computational power or a huge data set. This enhanced the accuracy gained by using ensemble learning techniques \[ 14 - 16 \], although the technique created difﬁculties in model tuning and model comprehension.
