## 3 **Proposed Methodology **

## Projections made in the framework give an account of future criminal events, in terms

of identiﬁcation of a particular region and timeframe, as well as the likelihood and the type of crime. The constructed system is based on the Random Forest algorithm due to its high classiﬁcation accuracy and the ability to handle complex, non-linear data simultaneously, with a strong capacity to deal with complex datasets while remaining interpretable. The model operates as a structured multi-step model that integrates data manipulation processes and the quality of performance is assured.

## • The ﬁrst process is aimed at receiving full crime database data in law enforcement

systems and reporting on the crime in the public domain as well as API data solutions to analyze the historical and current trends. The whole forecasting process commences by use of this data collection. - The analysis and patterns of crime data in time and space are identiﬁed with the aid of  several visual and statistical tools during this stage. The analysis identiﬁes different trends whereby the data indicates seasonal changes and active hotspots and abnormal crime incidences. The patterns identiﬁed aid in engineering characteristics and choice of models to establish prediction that targets particular regions. - Phase of Data Preprocessing The stage of Data Preprocessing performs the required  cleaning and pre-processing of raw data towards making both it consistent and reliable. The data preparation procedure encompasses value inference of the absent points - Sisodia et al.

alongside variable conversion of the categories into the numbers along with mandatory feature scaling methods. The required preprocessing processes result in enhanced efﬁciency in learning and the precision in the model. - The model acquires more functionality due to new features that are produced in the  Feature Engineering processes. The statistician takes the frequency of crime by time of day, the hotspot index, and the crime-population ratio to generate the new derived features that recognize the variables of occurrence rate according to the crime patterns. The data segmentation allows a performance evaluation of the model on new data points which is free of bias hence allowing the model to establish its generalizable value even outside the training data.\\ - Based on their results in the evaluation process, the multiple classiﬁcation models evaluated are Decision Trees, along with Logistic Regression, Support Vector  Machines (SVM), and Random Forest due to their performance statistics. The reason why random Forest is the last model selection is that it gives the best levels of performance in conjunction with good resistance to overﬁtting at the same time having simple interpretability. - Random Forest model is created by training a set of decision trees using the training data set. The ﬁnal model forecast is based on tree outcomes of majority voting  techniques that can improve the accuracy and avoid the bias of the model on results. - The evaluation of the model's predictive effectiveness is conducted using accuracy,  precision, recall, F1-score, and the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC) measurement. The performance metrics put in place deﬁne the performance of the model as per the operational needs required in real crime activity prediction. - A grid search procedure optimizes the model performance by conducting parameter adjustment operations. The model optimization process requires adjustments to  parameters including the tree depth and split sample threshold alongside the selected tree count. - The model provides an evaluation of the variables that contribute most to crime  prediction results. The most consequential elements for crime prediction include time of day, geographic location, type of crime and prior incident frequency.

## 4 **Architecture Technique **

The crime forecasting system utilizes multiple machine learning algorithms because they specialize at processing structured crime data while performing classiﬁcation operations. The system employed separate predictive models and ensemble combinations to achieve desirable prediction accuracy together with clear interpretation. This part explains the main three model architectures which compose our system. **4.1 ** **Decision Tree Architecture **

Decision trees act as the base structure in our predictive framework because they deliver outstanding interpretability for investigators. The binary decision nodes in Fig. 2 function as hierarchical elements to perform a set of questions about input features such as "Is the

Advancing Urban Security: A Random Forest Approach to Predictive **Fig. 2 ** Diagram of Decision Tree

crime occurring at night?" The framework checks whether the area falls under identiﬁed active crime zones.

The training detects optimal separation criteria through information gain analysis which uses Gini Impurity as its main split criterion measure. Each node split within this approach decreases class entropy to make subsets increasingly homogeneous as the tree branches become deeper. The transparency aspect of Decision Trees allows users without technical backgrounds to track the workﬂow which connects features to crime category decisions. Tests revealed that Decison Trees used independently show susceptibility to overﬁtting despite their strong interpretability characteristics. Regularization techniques are necessary for the model to avoid memorization of training data since minimal sample requirements and pruning were absent leading to inferior performance across varied crime datasets. **4.2 ** **Random Forest Architecture **

To address the inherent instability of individual Decision Trees, we implemented Random Forest as our primary classiﬁcation architecture. As depicted in Fig. 3, this ensemble method constructs multiple decision trees (typically 100-500 in our implementation), each trained on randomized subsets of both data and features.

Random Forest architecture implements three essential operations to achieve its success.

- The random sampling phase of Bootstrap Aggregation (Bagging) creates separate  tree models with beneﬁcial variations in the analysis. - Part of the random feature selection method includes picking a subset of features  randomly when splitting nodes to improve model diversity while lowering betweentree correlations. - A democratic voting process merges tree outputs into one prediction which enhances  prediction accuracy and stability simultaneously.

The ensemble technique produces remarkable bias-variance equilibrium which proves useful for crime prediction tasks involving multidimensional non-linear patterns. - Sisodia et al. **Fig. 3 ** Diagram of Random Forest

The interpretability of Random Forests remains practical because stakeholders can utilize feature importance analysis to establish which variables create the most signiﬁcant impact on predictions. **4.3 ** **Complementary Model Architectures **

We primarily selected our main architectural design as Random Forest but we combined several other models to achieve performance benchmarks and enhance speciﬁc analytical capabilities.

As a beneﬁt, the binary crime prediction system beneﬁts with the Logistic Regression, as it builds a simple probabilistic classiﬁer. This type of architecture classiﬁes without the use of regression by applying its sigmoid function, which yields results with probabilities between 0 and 1. The linear decision boundary of the model has been used as a natural yardstick to evaluate more complex models.

- Naive Bayes architecture utilizes the Bayes Theorem to derive prior distributions and  combinations of likelihoods, ultimately leading to the best crime type classiﬁcation. Naive Bayes was characterized by great success despite its use of the assumption that all features are independent. - Linear Regression takes feature engineering and correlation analysis to the instrumental level, but fails to be applicable, especially to classiﬁcation problems. The system  created meaningful thresholds to categorize data and prepare features through its analysis of linear patterns between numerical data and crime data.

The interrelation of orthogonal processing units determines operational ﬂexibility by explainable functional options between the speedy analysis system and the comprehensive analysis of criminal patterns.

## 5 **Result and Discussion **

The proposed system incorporates temporal, spatial, and socio-economic characteristics in conjunction with historical crime data to produce precise forecasts of potential crime occurrences. There is a need to have access to law enforcement agencies with data processing systems that are capable of managing large amounts of information effectively and without favoritism, but produce accurate ﬁndings. The need to use Random Forest was informed by the fact that it imparts a high level of performance on difﬁcult data, which involved analyzing crime data in terms of both numerical and categorical values. Random Forest employs a learning process to develop a number of decision trees that integrate their respective results to produce ﬁnal predictions. The model is based on the majority voting of its group of decision trees in determining the crime class. The method also results in an increased level of accuracy, helping the model resist the overﬁtting effect. The forest decision trees, are trained on the data subset using randomly selected features that create a resilient model since such an arrangement does not lead to certain distortions in data.

Random Forest demonstrated excellent performance in analyzing a set of crime parameters, including crime time, type, site, area density, and socioeconomic variables. The in-built feature importance analysis of the model highlighted important predictive elements that helped identify the pattern and develop preventive measures. The capability to understand the existence of meaningful associations and the uncovering of speciﬁc reasons presented direct beneﬁts to the decision-maker in the context of using the models in policing tasks. The beneﬁt of using this approach is stability. The system was able to give reliable predictions even with small changes in its input data, which is good functionality when dealing with data whose inaccuracy is known. Ensemble design enables the system to mitigate faults in data, resulting in consistent outputs when presented with different situations.

The Random Forest-based crime prediction model produced superior outcomes than baseline algorithms when used in training and testing conditions. All vital evaluation metrics demonstrated high scores by the system in precision, accuracy, recall and F1score assessments. The learning method of aggregation with heterogeneous features capabilities produced strong prediction reliability and generalization capabilities for unseen data.

The Random Forest classiﬁcation model outperformed all other models because it obtained 86.7% accuracy alongside 84.3% precision and 85.8% recall and 85.0% F1score according to Table 2. The ﬁndings reinforce the chosen decision making process and support existing research conducted by Lima and Karabiyik \[ 4 \] and Ibrahim et al. \[ 6 \] which found ensemble methods to be superior at predicting crime. The Decision Tree showed an 8% reduction in performance metrics as it worked with less clarity than Random Forest. Random Forest established its superiority through superior results compared to Decision Trees since ensemble methods help prevent overﬁtting and address non-linear patterns in crime data. The results of this analysis conﬁrmed how Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes exhibited inferior performance due to linear models and independence assumptions not functioning well with multidimensional crime data. ## 6 **Conclusion **

## With the proposed model, which is based on the implementation of Random Forest,

crime forecasting is performed using structured multi-feature crime data to create robust predictions. It is a system that employs ensemble learning in order to ensure the correct, interpretable, and ﬂexible predictions that meet the necessary requirements of the public safety programs adopted by law enforcement agencies. The system is reliable across various environments because it effectively manages high-dimensional, complex information. The system has the data handling facilities that allow it to increase its capacity without interfering with the optimal operations of the system. The Random Forest algorithm does not overﬁt by nature, resulting in effective generalization and enabling the system to make accurate predictions, regardless of new emerging trends. This system is stable and does not allow the change in the input data to make signiﬁcant changes in the decision-making, thereby providing reliable outputs to assist professionals in ensuring that smarter crimes do not occur.

## 7 **Future Scope **

## The crime forecasting technique shows great potential to evolve into operational applica

tions that will increase its range. The accuracy and speed of the system can be improved by linking with real-time data streams from IoT systems, social media platforms, and response networks in emergency situations. Investigational research on deep learning models ought to be conducted to describe and model diverse temporal-spatial patterns. More context-aware insights would be obtained in the system containing the factors on the basis of the demographic data and economic conditions and environmental factors. This type of decision-support system would be deployed in the form of mobile or webdelivery, which supports the work of law enforcement agencies in proactive policing endeavors. The collaboration of the organizations between the urban planners and the public safety department will improve the strategies preventing crime and the distribution of resources adequately.

## Cybersecurity in the Digital Age

**A Comprehensive Review of Emerging Threats ** **and Defense Mechanisms **

Nagalakshmi Panchakatla 1, Kondragunta Rama Krishnaiah 2, D. Rammohan Reddy 3, - Kanthi Kumar 4, Swathi Nelavalli 5, and Kuppani Sathish 6( B )

**Abstract. ** This has made cybersecurity highly signiﬁcant nowadays, as online technology and constant network connectivity have made it essential to the security of businesses. The volume, extent and magnitude of cyber attacks have also expanded due to the digital transformation that is emerging in various ﬁelds. This review paper provides the full description of cybersecurity shifts and we outline the recent threats, in particular we have seen an increase in attacks by ransomware, zero-day exploits, country-based phishing and exploitation. Another aspect that is presented in the text is that emerging technologies (cloud computing, IoT and AI) are posing alternative threats that morning cybersecurity is not capable of addressing. Because of this, the approaches employed in defense are rapidly evolving. This paper examines recent security tools, such as detection of threats with the help of AI, blockchain-based security frameworks, Zero Trust and quantum computer resistance. In addition, the inﬂuence of rules and guidelines on increasing cybersilience is taken into account. Integrating the facts found in the recent publications, real-life examples and knowledge of the cybersecurity industry, this review provides the full picture of the current trends and proposes potential future steps to be taken in practice and research. The ﬁndings indicate that it is important to employ ﬂexible, swift and group strategies to support the security of the digital structure in the world.

## 1 **Introduction **

Digital transformation is the key to economic growth in the 21st century, social relations, and new ideas. People, groups and authorities have signiﬁcantly changed the way they work with such innovations as cloud computing, IoT, AI, blockchain and 5G \[ 1 \]. However, simultaneously, it is this massive shift to digital that has created excessive security threats that we have never encountered. The rise in the number of data breaches, ransomware attacks and cyber spying has put the cybersecurity requirement on the top of the priority list in all disciplines.

Due to the digitized era, everyone now is more connected than ever before. Computer systems have been applied to homes, industry, health care and government and they are getting more interconnected. Even though online afﬁliations enable organizations to perform more efﬁciently and effectively, it also presents companies with numerous risks. The threats today are far greater and more organized than they appeared to be in the past and the sources of the threats are equally varied as amateurs, organized crime organizations and nation states. Cybersecurity threats these days are very broad and include social engineering, ransomware, APTs, supplier and zero-day bugs attacks.

The current situation reveals that cybersecurity should be enhanced. SolarWinds breach, the Colonial pipeline breach and a series of healthcare breaches have demonstrated how the loopholes in cybersecurity may lead to such issues as the loss of money, jeopardizing the national defense, and inﬂicting harm on population health. Such situations prove that cybersecurity must be taken into account by every member of an organization as now it assists in managing risks and safeguarding people.

Meanwhile, the COVID-19 threat continues to expand due to the emergence of digital tools. Nowadays, there is an increasing number of individuals who work remotely, groups of people work in a virtual environment and use digital services, but the pace of change is much higher than the innovations intended to improve security systems and methods can be implemented. Many organizations lacked effective cybersecurity plans as they migrated to remote systems and became easy targets of phishing, malware and an innumerable amount of logins. Due to this change, it was evident that we require the new cybersecurity tools to defend us in a boundaryless world.

Firewalls, antivirus programs and models that rely only on borders are showing their weakness in the face of new threats. Adopting cloud infrastructure and edge computing points out the need for a change in security approaches. For this reason, security methods in the military have advanced to include smart technology, blockchain security and tight access measures through the ZTA model \[ 2 \]. They indicate that organizations are switching to taking action against cyber threats ahead of their emergence.

Following rules and regulations for cybersecurity is more important today. Laws and cybersecurity rules such as the GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA and NIST Cybersecurity Framework are being enforced by various governments and international organizations. Although these guidelines are important, they are often not very effective due to fast technological changes and divided regulatory systems. It is also important to note that being compliant does not guarantee security, because there have been many security breaches in organizations that were compliant.

This review aims at analyzing cybersecurity within the digital environment by examining the threats and the means of mitigation. The coverage begins with an explanation Cybersecurity in the Digital Age: A Comprehensive Review

on how cyber threats have evolved and how they are becoming more challenging and important. The next section of the paper examines the sophisticated methods and technologies employed to avert such threats including application of AI, machine learning, blockchain and quantum-safe encryption. In addition, the paper examines the regulations and policies governing cybersecurity across the globe.

**Fig. 1. ** Evolution of Cybersecurity Threats in the Digital Age

Figure 1 evidently shows that digital transformation is transforming cybersecurity threats and the cybersecurity defenses. At this point, criminals employ sophisticated tactics and the former framework of borders and reactive cyberdefense is unable to deal with them \[ 1 \]. Due to digital technologies like cloud computing, IoT, AI and remote work infrastructure, the list of potential attacks increased, and new categories of threats are being built, including AI attacks, main pipeline compromise, and threats, which are being built with the help of quantum computing \[ 2 \]. Through the SolarWinds breach and the Colonial Pipeline attack, the evolution may be observed as the current cyber threat may grow beyond business silos to the extent of affecting the country overall infrastructure and national security. Due to this fact, cybersecurity has transferred to active measures based on the Zero Trust Architecture, artiﬁcial intelligence in the detection of threats and cryptography prepared to the threats of the future, which is backed by in-depth regulations to establish minimum security standards worldwide. The purpose of this review is to see where cybersecurity defenses are currently deﬁcient and describe the future steps necessary in research. Since cybersecurity brings together different topics, it needs experts from technology, laws, policies and behavioral sciences to collaborate. Therefore, it underlines the signiﬁcance of involving various groups to handle cyber threats as they keep evolving. It points out that since there is a growing shortage of cybersecurity experts, we need to focus more on educating people, raising awareness and developing new workers.

With our society becoming more dependent on technology, cybersecurity should not be seen as an extra task. It has to be included in the structure of systems, processes and governance at the beginning of the project. As we depend more on technology, the dangers of cyber incidents go up as well. Cybersecurity touches on many aspects such as business, society and government and so, it should be managed actively and long-term. So, this paper provides a key resource to help viewers understand where cybersecurity stands today and how it should adjust to new digital changes. By gathering recent studies, current best practices from the industry and details about current cybersecurity laws, this review aims to give researchers, practitioners and decision-makers the tools to deal with the complicated cybersecurity landscape today.

## 2 **Cyber Threat Landscape in the Digital Age **

The digital change in society has helped us be more efﬁcient, connected and use data to make choices. Nevertheless, it has opened up new opportunities for cyber criminals to be more advanced. Since the world is more connected nowadays, attackers are taking advantage of new technologies to discover weaknesses, change information and attack speciﬁc organizations. These cyber threats have grown from simple viruses to advanced types that can overcome the best cyber protection systems \[ 3 \]. **2.1 ** **Evolution of Cyber Threats **

Just like technology, cyber threats have developed with time. At the start of the internet, people were mostly concerned about trivial viruses and hacking for fame. Nowadays, the types of cyber threats involve ﬁnancial criminals, activist hackers, terrorists and cyber attackers backed by nations. Many threats are not easy to spot, keep coming and are able to get past regular border protection. The goals today include gaining ﬁnancial beneﬁts, stealing ideas and secrets, interfering with politics and spying on databases.

Today's cyber attackers rely on automation with AI to search for weaknesses, run phishing attacks and make malware change its form. Additionally, cybercrime-as-aservice (CaaS) allows people who are not experts to rent ransomware or buy access to accounts that have been compromised which makes things more dangerous. For this reason, cybersecurity experts have to deal with both more attacks and threat actors that are better at staying hidden. **2.2 ** **Classiﬁcation of Cyber Threats **

Healthcare stands out as a target because it uses a lot of old systems and tech connected in the same network. If a hospital is hit by ransomware, important treatments may have to be put on hold and the safety of patients could be put at risk. In 2021, the HSE in Ireland was hit by a ransomware attack and services remained closed for many weeks.

Finance: Phishing, credential stufﬁng and fake transactions are major threats that ﬁnancial ﬁrms have to deal with. Because they offer direct beneﬁts and collect sensitive personal information, these organizations are major targets. Instances of attacks like the Bangladesh Bank Heist (2016) show that ﬁnancial systems around the globe are exposed to threats.

Many malevolent groups supported by governments try to target and undermine important agencies in the public sector. For example, the Stuxnet worm went after Iran's nuclear sites and the SolarWinds incident invaded the networks of U.S. federal organizations. Evidently, these attacks are crafted cleverly to be hard to ﬁnd, so authorities must work together to identify and respond to them.

ICS systems control vital areas such as the power, manufacturing and water industries by using OT systems more and more linked to the internet. Missiles often do not have today's safety measures and can be ruined by malware or unauthorized access which might harm national protection and security. **2.4 ** **Emerging Threat Vectors **

Response to new technology is causing the emergence of additional cyber threats.

AI is used by attackers to make fake videos, launch phishing campaigns and ﬁnd out about security weaknesses so they can exploit them in bulk.

## 3 **Emerging Cybersecurity Challenges **

As the cyber threats continue to become more advanced and frequent, the cybersecurity community is forced to manage new issues that go beyond technology. These challenges are driven by technological advances, actions of threats, new laws, and overall unreadiness, in general. As the organizations modernize their security system they also deal with threats in a dynamic digital world where fast response does not work effectively. This section outlines the largest issues that are going to deﬁne the future of cybersecurity and complicate the process of dealing with threats. **3.1 ** **Increasing Sophistication of Cyber Attacks **

They are now using innovative technologies such as machine learning, deepfakes and automation to carry out targeted attacks that are hard to detect. Many times, these attacks are hard to detect, so they allow intruders to take much information for a long period. APTs have become increasingly common lately, indicating that attackers are now planning more strategic, long-term actions. Moreover, these malicious programs and ﬁleless attacks avoid typical antivirus programs by changing their patterns and running directly in main memory.

**3.2 ** **Expanded Attack Surface due to Digital Transformation **

Due to more people using cloud, IoT, mobile and edge, there are now more points where attacks can occur. Organizations have to secure information that is kept outside their direct care such as through third-party apps, remote devices and personal gadgets owned by employees. Because data and applications are scattered, it becomes easier to miss gaps in visibility and lose powerful security systems. Since organizations are using hybrid and remote work models, security policies have to change for perimeters that are not clearly deﬁned. **3.3 ** **Security Skills Gap and Resource Constraints **

More and more, it is clear that there is a worldwide shortage of cybersecurity specialists. Following reports in the industry, there are millions of unﬁlled cybersecurity jobs due to people not having the proper training, awareness or skills needed \[ 6 \]. Because of this shortage, it is hard for organizations to watch for threats as they happen, regularly check their security or put the best security habits in place. SMEs usually do not have the resources for both expensive workers and costly tools which makes them more likely to be the targets of cyber attacks. - Panchakatla et al.

ity models that can cause problems when assigning blame. Common issues still include insecure use of resources in the cloud, weak access controls and improper handling of applications program interfaces. In addition, having different tenants in a system raises the chances of data being leaked and attacked from other tenants. Having workloads on IaaS, PaaS and SaaS clouds and meeting security regulations only adds more challenges to cloud security.

## 4 **Modern Defense Mechanisms and Strategies **

## Increasing cyber threats these days have necessitated the organizations to change the

approach to cyber security. Regular, perimeter defense models are unfortunately not sufﬁcient to be applied in the current environment with cloud, mobile and Internet of Cybersecurity in the Digital Age: A Comprehensive Review

Things systems. Instead, the ﬁrms are turning to new technologies, best strategies and coordinated risk management to safeguard their systems against cyber threats \[ 7 \]. This part gives us a glimpse into the innovations in defense techniques and plans that will secure us in future. **4.1 ** **Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) **

Zero Trust is based on the concept of not trusting anything and ensuring all access is checked. Conventional models place their faith in the network perimeter whereas ZTA regularly controls identity of mobile and devices regardless of whether they are in-premises or remote. The system has access control based on elaborate policies, contemporary factors and the least privilege principle. This kind of architecture is the most required in scenarios where remote personnel are involved, web-based services and mobile gadgets since the protection of the perimeter is insufﬁcient. It assists companies to minimize their danger of movement at lateral during information security violations and provides added control over valuable information \[ 8 \].

**4.2 ** **Cybersecurity and Artiﬁcial Intelligence and Machine Learning **

Cybersecurity tools have now employed AI and ML to detect threats, uncharacteristic activity, and respond to attacks instantly. machine learning models have the ability to handle massive amounts of data to highlight cyber threats that are not identiﬁed by people. Under AI, behavioral analytics software follows the activity of users and entities and notiﬁes about any suspicious alterations that may signify the possibility of an intrusion. In addition, the reaction time is accelerated when some of the security uses AI to automatize certain investigations, enhance the investigation procedure and contribute to forecasting possible threats.

**4.3 ** **Extended Detection and Response (XDR) and Endpoint Detection ** **and Response (EDR) **

They monitor any occurrences on the system and gadgets on a routine basis. These tools identify anything suspicious with the help of telemetry and behavioral analysis. When using XDR, one can implement the same approach with the network, endpoint, cloud and identity systems as a response to the threat \[ 9 \]. XDR assists teams in security to manage and identify threats more effectively through the use of various side data.

Table 3 presents six of the best modern strategies in cybersecurity and demonstrates that each of them contributes to a ﬂexible and multiple-layered defence model. All in all, these strategies assist in developing security systems that react effectively, get ahead of problems and think intelligently in order to contain the current emerging cyber terror. Overall, managing cybersecurity in the postmodern world is based on a strategy that is both informative and immediate-reactive. As shown in Table 3, AI, blockchain and Zero Trust are signiﬁcantly stronger than legacy systems when they are applied along with strong identity management and continuous monitoring. Organizations must also be committed, have competent teams and alter their strategies when required. The next section will describe the policies and overview required to make these defense strategies across the world and across various sectors, in order to be standardized and supported. - Panchakatla et al.

## 5 **Regulatory Frameworks and Compliance **

## With the constantly changing cybersecurity, there are regulatory standards and rules that

guarantee all organizations to secure sensitive information and remain trustworthy. Due to the increasing complexity and harmful nature of cyber threats, different governments and non-governmental organizations have implemented regulations and standards to see companies install powerful security protocols, uphold the privacy of users and effectively handle security breaches.

## These laws do not only legalize cybersecurity behaviors but also create a standard and

responsibility, transforming the whole world to become more proﬁcient at cybersecurity. However, the laws and policies in the country are so diverse in various regions that a signiﬁcant number of businesses ﬁnd it difﬁcult to meet all the demands.

## 5.1 **Importance of Cybersecurity Regulations **

## Organizations under cybersecurity regulations must use advanced risk management sys

tems, install proper safety measures and put incident response plans in place. Being compliant with rules and regulations ensures customer information is safe, fraud is discouraged and the business keeps going. Failing to comply may bring legal actions, ruin a business's reputation, cost money and sometimes result in criminal charges in certain areas.

## When it comes to healthcare, ﬁnance, defense and critical infrastructure, strict reg

ulations are crucial because a mistake can be disastrous. Naturally, protecting patient information involves upholding strict laws in healthcare, including HIPAA in the United States. In the same way, ﬁnancial institutions must achieve security expectations given by the GLBA and PCI DSS. Cybersecurity in the Digital Age: A Comprehensive Review

In each region and industry, the rules might vary, though common elements are privacy, obtaining consent from users, reporting security incidents and using security as a main strategy. Overall, these requirements add up to various compliance tasks that organizations have to complete as the world grows more joined. - Panchakatla et al. **5.3 ** **Challenges in Compliance Management **

Although adhering to regulation may be helpful, it poses signiﬁcant challenges to large international organizations. Due to regional variations in rules, a company might have to develop two or more approaches towards data governance and deal with the additional legal problems because of it. Similarly, GDPR at times makes data to be stored within a particular area, however, a similar law in the U.S. called the Cloud Act allows law enforcement agencies to gain access to and disseminate data that causes certain concerns regarding legal uniformity.

Then compliance is costly and is associated with numerous complexities. Organization should put money in the ﬁeld of auditing, employee training, documentation, expert attorneys and innovative software to meet the rules. The regulatory compliance should be veriﬁed, monitored and modiﬁed intermittently as the law can change any time as well as the threats.

**5.4 ** **Use of Compliance to Enhance Cybersecurity Posture **

Compliance is a necessity when adhering to laws; it will enhance security, and minimize risks. These regulations suggest companies to employ a predetermined strategy to manage risks, continuously gain and take an active part in protecting themselves through controls \[ 11 \]. By embracing compliance as their cybersecurity strategy, organizations are likely to reap the beneﬁts of good governance, relationship of trust with the stakeholders and prompt responses to cyberattacks. Adherence to own and other compliance guides will facilitate internal audit, external assessment by other companies and insurance claims requirements.

Cybersecurity regulations need to be brought closer together as worldwide sharing of data keeps growing and cybercrime continues proliferating. Among the groups that are now calling upon the establishment of cybersecurity standards that can recognize independence of the various countries are the United Nations, OECD and the G7. By consolidating all the standards into a single unit, it becomes easier to follow the standards by everyone and will eliminate duplication of efforts and this will see more countries cooperate in combating cyber related problems. However, the problem of reaching agreement between all the parties is a difﬁcult question in the context of geopolitics and laws.

## 6 **Conclusion **

As threats to cybersecurity constantly evolve and integrate with advanced technologies, it is challenging in numerous ways nowadays. New threats such as sophisticated malware, greater vulnerabilities through work with cloud and IoT, and a lack of global skills are described in this review as issues that hamper the defense work. Moreover, it has checked new defense technologies such as Zero Trust network with the help of AI, marking out danger, and securing with blockchain. Moreover, it has also been indicated that in order to be accountable, data privacy and organizational survivability, stringent regulations and requirements in the industry are essential. Given that cyber threats are global and encompass numerous nations, it is quite challenging even to large organizations to deal with the number of differing regulations. However, adhering to and adopting Cybersecurity in the Digital Age: A Comprehensive Review

## these guidelines enhances the level of safety and establishes trust within the responsi

ble parties. Overall, cybersecurity management implies the utilization of sophisticated technologies, hiring of talented individuals, the application of stringent regulations and the promotion of collaboration between various nations. Such a comprehensive strategy assists organizations to plan, identify and deal with cyber issues before they destroy valuable digital devices and data.

## 7 **Future Trends **

## Artiﬁcial intelligence and quantum computing are also automation, which is likely to

make a dent in the cybersecurity industry and bring new security solutions and potential types of attack. The use of such methods as blockchain and federated learning might render it difﬁcult to employ such attackers to manipulate or access personal data. In addition, unifying international cybersecurity will decrease the hard work of compliance and facilitate cooperation among countries in ﬁghting cybercrime. Nonetheless, to remain prepared to ﬁght cyber attacks, there is still a need to assist in developing cyber security competencies in learners and employees. Cybersecurity will be used as well as physical security, and AI-based analytics will help to make security systems more prepared and stable. Companies that are receptive to such future trends and are ﬂexible will protect their digital resources in the best possible way because technology is rapidly changing.

**Abstract. ** How to maximize shareholders' returns has been a research focus of ﬁnancial discipline. Standard machine learning algorithms tend to fail to discover hidden temporal structures, and thus new strategies are needed. The study introduces a deep learning model that begins with a dimension reduction step for feature space by t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE). Then the compressed representations are projected onto images by Markov Transition Field (MTF) technique. The Vision Transformer (ViT) induces informative embeddings from such images and passes them to a modiﬁed sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model that employs an attention mechanism to extract temporal dependencies. The LSTM-produced embeddings are then predicted using Fully Connected Neural Networks (FCNN), VGG models, and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The comparative analysis assesses the efﬁcacy of different models based on examination of the compressed feature space outcome. Imbalance in the dataset is addressed by the use of the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) that creates a balanced label distribution. Twenty stocks from seven leading sectors of the Indian capital market provide the source of the test data for the proposed methodology. In various market sectors trend classiﬁcation registered accuracy levels greater than 80%. Deep learning methods demonstrate their capacity to signiﬁcantly push forward stock market classiﬁcation by creating an extendable and consistent predictive model.

**Keywords: ** Technical Indicator · convolution neural network · t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) · MTF · Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE)

## 1 **Introduction **

## Stocks are one of the most popular ﬁnancial products due to their potential for providing

substantial returns at a high risk and their open trading environment. In the hopes of earning substantial proﬁts through accurate price predictions, many investors are drawn to the stock market \[ 1 \]. It is quite challenging to forecast stock prices. Market dynamics,

© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026 - Virdee et al. (Eds.): ICAIN 2025, LNNS 1931, pp. 79-93, 2026.  <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-23314-1\_6> V.K. Pandey et al.

important socioeconomic events, investor mood, company activities, and macroeconomic conditions are some of the factors that inﬂuence stock prices. Predicting stock prices is a crucial yet extremely complicated area of research because of its complex nature. In the past, econometric and statistical models were used to try and predict stock prices. Despite the fact that techniques like ARIMA and GARCH-ARIMA frequently fail to capture the dynamic and non-stationary features of the stock market. Real ﬁnancial data seldom satisﬁes the assumptions of classic models, such as linearity and steady behaviour.

Due to the quick development of computer technology since the 1970s, researchers have been working harder to apply methods from machine learning to stock price prediction. Large-scale data and complicated, non-linear relationships are better modeled by machine learning algorithms \[ 2 \]. Deep learning techniques have recently gained popularity due to their remarkable efﬁcacy; they often exhibit higher prediction accuracy and dynamism than traditional techniques \[ 3 - 5 \]. One of the most common types of complicated time series is stock market data, which is characterized by ongoing volatility, particularly during trading periods, and susceptibility to unanticipated outside events. These lead to tremendously complex and changeable datasets that are very difﬁcult to process using conventional modelling techniques. As a result, research has concentrated on two areas: selecting the most appropriate characteristics to train models on and enhancing the quality of predictive models.

An essential foundation for preliminary economic study is provided by econometric models. However, econometric models often ignored the impact of externalities and depended on rigid assumptions about the characteristics of the data. Because machine learning and deep learning are adaptable and can ﬁnd hidden patterns in data, they are used increasingly often in modern research. For regression and classiﬁcation, neural nets have consistently outperformed traditional models \[ 3, 6 \]. Additionally, recent research has expanded the sets of data used in forecasting to include political indicators, macroeconomic factors, and investor emotion in order to increase precision. Nevertheless, despite these signiﬁcant advancements, the existing approaches still have signiﬁcant drawbacks. These models could be ignoring the larger picture even when using social media data to gauge investor sentiment. Techniques like PCA and LDA are used to minimize complexity while processing large amounts of data. However, PCA loses important information, especially when the data isn't linear, while LDA struggles to comprehend how words link in text. That can lead to weaker results \[ 7, 8 \].

By taking the motivation from above literature, to enhance the accuracy of stock price pattern classiﬁcation, this study proposes a novel paradigm for market trend classiﬁcation by combining deep learning models with advanced data transformations in the Indian ﬁnance sector. We ﬁrst enrich the raw ﬁnancial time series data by calculating several technical indicators to capture important market signals. The high-dimensional data is then compressed using t-SNE to preserve the important structures while reducing dimensionality. After compression, the data is transformed into Markov Transition Field (MTF) images, representing the temporal patterns visually. We derive embeddings of these MTF images using Vision Transformer (ViT) models. These embeddings are then fed into a sequence-to-sequence LSTM model with a local attention mechanism based on which the model can pay attention to the most essential parts of the sequence. The

Stock Price Direction Forecasting Using Compressed Feature Space

last layer obtained embeddings are then classiﬁed with models such as Fully Connected Neural Networks (FCNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Inception networks or VGG models and Support vector machines (SVM). A special algorithm (we developed a custom index) is employed to classify the data as 'buy', 'sell', and 'hold'. To handle the issue of class imbalance, which is caused by nature of stock price, SMOTE is used before classiﬁcation. In the present study we tested our method using data of twenty stocks from Indian Stock Market. Experiments have shown that our achievable accuracy being 80% for stock price patterns classiﬁcation, and our method can improve the forecasting accuracy of the stock price and provide the decision support for the investors. Our study investigates complex embedding-driven deep learning methodologies, providing an organized trading framework intended to reduce risk-to-return ratios and enhance predictive model resilience, in contrast to current methods that mainly concentrate on generic stock movement prediction. This method helps to improve stock market research with a more data-driven viewpoint by utilizing feature compression, image-based analysis, and deep learning architectures to deliver insightful information for medium- and short-term investment planning.

This paper is structured as follows: Section 2 reviews past research and methodologies related to ﬁnancial forecasting. Section 3 details the proposed methodology, including model architecture, labelling strategy, and MTF image creation. Section 4 presents experimental results, followed by a comparison with existing models. In Sect. 5 mention the Discussion and Finally, Sect. 6 concludes the paper and discusses future research directions. **1.1 ** **Literature Review **

The ﬁnancial industry has progressively sought more accurate forecasting models, evolving from traditional methods like basic technical analysis to more sophisticated, datadriven approaches utilizing machine learning techniques \[ 2, 9, 10 \]. While models like ARIMA have traditionally supported ﬁnancial forecasting, they often encounter limitations due to their inherent design. In recent years, machine learning algorithms-such as decision trees and supporting vector machines-along with various neural network architectures, have been adopted for this purpose. These models can be economically sensitive to noise and generally have high feature engineering requirements. Since then, better deep learning models have been created as substitutes.

Initially designed for image processing, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are becoming more and more popular in the ﬁnancial industry. Well-known models like VGG16, ResNet50, and Inception have already been pre-trained on enormous data sets like ImageNet, establishing new benchmarks for performance \[ 3, 11, 12 \].  The  task  of developing highly precise and computationally light models is considerably simpliﬁed by the reﬁnement of pre-trained deep learning models. CNNs are better able to identify investment measures due to developments that convert time series data into picture formats, such as Markov Transition Fields (MTF) and Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) \[ 3 \]. Because convolutional layers are highly effective at identifying important trends in stock price movements, this modiﬁcation is particularly beneﬁcial when applying deep V.K. Pandey et al.

learning architectures to ﬁnancial time-series data. However, the singular unpredictability, noise, and non-linearity found in ﬁnancial markets present unique challenges that require more innovative solutions.

However, a major obstacle to applying such models in the ﬁnancial industry is managing the intrinsic temporal characteristics of simple time series data. Although they are still in the early stages of research, methods like GAF and MTF show potential. These methods turn ﬁnancial time series into pictures so that signiﬁcant patterns may be found for prediction using deep learning models. Although it represents an important achievement, there are still problems with using pre-trained deep learning frameworks when combined with data transformation techniques for ﬁnancial prediction. Financial markets frequently exhibit volatility, with little adjustments to input parameters producing signiﬁcant variations in outcomes. Even though pre-trained deep learning models excel at extracting features, they typically struggle to handle unforeseen patterns in ﬁnancial data sets.. By focusing on important data points that have a big impact on prediction results, attention mechanisms have become increasingly important in ﬁnancial market prediction in recent years. In 2020, Qiu et al. enhanced prediction accuracy by integrating an Attention Mechanism (AM) into a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model \[ 13, 14 \], Performance was further improved in 2022 when researchers used wavelet transforms to denoise historical stock prices before employing an LSTM-AM model \[ 15 \]. Originally developed for sequence modelling, transformers have also been studied for predicting stock movement. In \[ 16 \] demonstrated how well a transformer model enhanced with a multiGaussian prior predicted stock movement \[ 15 \]. Furthermore, Wang et al. demonstrated that transformers are more effective than conventional techniques for stock market index prediction, and \[ 13, 17 \] employed a transformer-LSTM hybrid model to forecast Chinese bank stock prices. Additionally, most models are made to forecast certain stocks or unique indexes, which limits their adaptability and usefulness. The precision of the model and structural optimization still has a lot of space for improvement.

In this study, we aim to bridge the gap by developing a trading system that utilizes a hybrid deep learning model integrated with MTF, focusing on sector-wise classiﬁcation of stock price patterns. This approach is designed to enhance trading signals for shortand long-term investments.

| 2.1 | Model Architecture |

In this section, we discuss the detailed method followed in the paper. We start with the system architecture given in "Fig. 1 ". **2.1 ** **Model Architecture **

In this study, we provide a novel approach to stock price uncertainty prediction using Yahoo Finance data in order to increase the predictive capability of our system. We developed a deep learning-based model structure that efﬁciently and systematically works

Stock Price Direction Forecasting Using Compressed Feature Space **Fig. 1 ** Overview of Proposed Methodology

with time-series data that has been MTF-transformed. We begin by adding characteristics taken from technical indicators, which provide useful information about volume and other signiﬁcant variables, to the data in order to enhance it. Following the usage of these technical features, we use t-SNE to compress the feature space while retaining the most important features. We then use compressed feature space data to generate MTF pictures from rolling window sequences. The image embeddings of the MTF representations are then extracted using a Vision Transformer (ViT) model. The ViT transforms the intricate patterns and exact movements of the MTF images into efﬁcient embeddings that precisely match the original stock movement. A multilayer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with a local attention mechanism is used to get the embeddings. The attention layer specializes in the most relevant parts in the sequences, enhancing network interpretability and accuracy, while the LSTM layers allow the model to understand sequential relationships between time steps. We utilize the ﬁnal LSTM outputs as the embeddings that best illustrate the compressed temporal dynamics in order to further promote the representations. These embeddings are then ﬂattened and fed into several machine learning and deep learning algorithms. The network subsequently makes use of thresholds produced by large price change quartiles to classify stock price action into three modes: BUY, HOLD, or SELL. By doing so, the model is guaranteed to make predictions that will closely mirror actual market behaviour. The overall system architecture is a strong pipeline that is capable of precisely predicting market movements through the integration of geographical, sequential, and contextual data. Measures like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score gave a comprehensive picture of the performance of the system and were evaluated on unseen data. The below subsections explain each part of this method in detail. "Fig. 2 " illustrates the overall structure of the general methodology. **2.2 ** **Labeling of Stock Close Prices **

In this research, we have labeled stock prices in this study using a method that relates to the percentage change in stock prices within a given rolling window. Relative differences V.K. Pandey et al.

**Fig. 2 ** Detailed Architecture of End-to-End Classiﬁcation Model

were calculated as the percentage difference between the ﬁrst and the last price of each window. The quartiles of these change values namely the 25 th,  50 th, and 75 th

percentiles were calculated. From these quartiles, the algorithm labeled each data point: 'BUY' for large positive changes, 'SELL' for large negative changes, and 'HOLD' for values in between the interquartile range. This approach facilitates systematic detection, classiﬁcation, and labeling of stock price changes. The general structure of the stock labeling process is depicted in "Fig. 3.

In addition to simple price tagging, we further enriched the dataset by adding a series of technical indicators, giving additional market context for tasks in subsequent predictions. **2.3 ** **Additional Features Via Technical Indicators **

To capture, we utilize well known set of technical indicators in the form of feature set to assist us in recognizing key market movements. Technical indicators, which are mathematical calculations, are utilized by traders to ﬁnd market state and recognize potential trading opportunities. Some of the technical indicators employed in this study are Bollinger Bands, stochastic oscillators, moving averages, the Relative Strength Index (RSI), and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD). To be precise, we used 15 technical indicators to identify trends, momentum, volatility, and overbought or oversold levels. All these indications were derived from past price and volume values. For instance, RSI detects the speed and size of price changes to gauge market conditions, whereas moving averages eliminate price ﬂuctuations to signify direction of trends. The incorporation of these technical indicators formed a high-dimensional feature space. To manage and analyze this complexity better, we employed dimensionality reduction techniques, as described below in the following subsection.

Stock Price Direction Forecasting Using Compressed Feature Space **Fig. 3 ** Labeling Method of Data **2.4 ** **Feature Compression **

In order to reduce the dimensionality of the technical indicator data and increase the visibility of its underlying structure, we used t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding (t-SNE). Translating high-dimensional data into a low-dimensional space (more often 2D or 3D) while trying to maintain the local neighbourhood relationships between data points of similar nature is a proper application for t-SNE, a non-linear dimensionality reduction method. We were able to determine patterns and clusters with which stock price activity is related using t-SNE on the technical indicators. These visualizations performed classiﬁcation by highlighting different groups of similar market patterns, such as bullish, bearish, or neutral trends. Second, and possibly the most signiﬁcant, t-SNE visualizations enhanced the model's capacity to identify different market circumstances and the comprehension of the data distribution, both of which are essential for precisely predicting stock prices. We next transformed the sequential data into pictures so that deep learning models could perform additional analysis because the feature space had been reduced to a lower dimensional representation.. **2.5 ** **Image Generation **

After t-SNE dimension reduction, we created MTF images to visualize the spatial and temporal dependencies in the stock price data. MTF images are formed by converting time-series data into 2D matrices wherein one dimension is time, and the other represents transition probabilities from quantized states formed from the original time series. Through this transformation, models are able to identify latent patterns and trends in sequential data that would otherwise be challenging to identify. V.K. Pandey et al.

In our approach, each rolling window of prelabeled stock price data augmented with technical indicators was constructed into a 2D MTF matrix. The matrices encapsulate the sequential dynamics of the stock prices while preserving crucial temporal dependencies. Transformation includes data normalization and encoding it into grid-based form that preserves time-dependent transition dynamics. Once generated, the MTF images served as the input to the deep model, which allowed the subtle patterns of trend changes, volatility regimes, and momentum bursts to be extracted. With the dense representation facilitated by MTF images, our model successfully detected and learned the pattern for both short-run ﬂuctuations and long-run market trends and enhanced stock price prediction performance by a signiﬁcant margin. The sample MTF image shown in "Fig. 4 ".

**Fig. 4 ** Sample of MTF Image with Compressed Feature Space **2.6 ** **SMOTE Technique for Imbalance Dataset **

After we had converted the data to images using the previous approach, we realized that there was an imbalance in the labels Buy, Sell, and Hold. This skewed distribution may bias the predictions and cause the model to overrepresent the majority class and ﬁnd it difﬁcult to detect important buying and selling signals accurately. In order to overcome this, we utilize SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique), which balances the dataset by creating new, realistic examples for the minority Buy and Sell signals instead of repeating the ones already present. SMOTE considers the individual features of these minority classes and produces artiﬁcial data points that incrementally fall into their patterns. Therefore, the data set is better balanced, making it possible for the model to learn effectively in all categories. This works greatly to improve prediction accuracy, especially in the identiﬁcation of proﬁtable market trends, which form the basis of informed trading decisions. The ﬁndings are then given in the following section.

## 3 **Dataset and Evaluation **

The dataset for this research includes daily stock rates for the following Indian stocks over the last ﬁve years such as: Adani Enterprises, Apollo Hospitals, Power Grid, Maruti Suzuki, Britannia, HCL Tech, and others. This data has been retrieved from Yahoo Finance, a reliable source for historical stock value data.

Each record in our dataset contains the date, open price, close price, highest price of the day, lowest price of the day, the number of shares transacted during the day, and the

Stock Price Direction Forecasting Using Compressed Feature Space

adjusted closing price. The closing price is utilized to create image-like constructions through Markov Transition Fields (MTF) transformations. The labels representing the trends we aim to forecast are generated using a window-based labeling process with a window size of 10 days. **3.1 ** **Experiment with Different Models **

In examining the performance of classiﬁcation against various model structures used for stock image data up sampled using Markov Transition Fields (MTF), different trends are observed for ﬁrms like Adani Enterprises, BPCL, and Power Grid Corporation. The Feedforward Neural Network (FNN) combined with the features of MTF-based compressed provides uniform and high performance across all three labels, 'Buy', 'Hold', and 'Sell', proving its stability and ability for generalization. Conversely, the VGG-type Convolution Neural Network (CNN) with MTF demonstrated better accuracy for the 'Buy' category but had relatively lower recall for the 'Hold' tag in some stocks, reﬂecting a compromise between label sensitivity and overall accuracy. In contrast, while Support Vector Machine (SVM) classiﬁer, although competitive in individual classes especially in classifying 'Hold' signals for Adani and BPCL, fell behind in recall and consistency for the 'Sell' class. These ﬁndings highlight that model selection is domainand priority-dependent: for use cases desiring fair performance per class, FCNN models with MTF embeddings are preferred; however, if better detection of 'Buy' signals is more important, CNN architecture can be more suitable. **3.2 ** **Analysis Via Different Models **

The performance comparison outcomes illustrate the performance advantage of Feedforward Convolution Neural Networks (FCNNs) combined with Markov Transition Field representations. According to Table 1, the FCNN and MTF model shows the highest average F1-scores across ﬁrms for robust performance in both precision and recall. For example, Adani has a very well-balanced proﬁle with an F1-score of 0.76 for 'Buy', 0.754 for 'Sell', and 0.776 for 'Hold'. Comparatively, Table 2 shows that the VGG-like CNN model, while yielding the highest F1-score of 0.803 for Adani's 'Hold' class, is less consistent across the other classes. Likewise, Table 3 indicates that the SVM with MTF model yields good F1-scores for the 'Hold' class but performs poorly in 'Sell' prediction, particularly for Power Grid with F1 score 0.715. These observations validate that MTF-based compressed features contribute to improved model performance on different architectures, but the FCNN based model always excels based on overall classiﬁcation stability. The outcome identiﬁes how ﬁne-tuned models utilizing MTF are superior compared to those without MTF. In subsequent work, pretrained transformerbased and hybrid architectures are sought to be explored with MTF to enhance model generalization and optimize stock movement classiﬁcation. V.K. ## 4 **Result **

**Fig. 5 ** Overall Accuracy and F1- Score of Different Model Integrated with MTF

In this research, we compared the performances of various machine learning models namely FCNN, VGG-based convolutional models, and SVM all combined with compressed feature representations extracted from MTF transformations. We evaluated these models based on how they classify stock price movement into three different categories: Buy, Hold, and Sell.

The outcomes, as shown in Table 4, indicate that FCNN, when combined with MTF, recorded the highest overall F1-Score of 0.7420 and accuracy of 0.7429, surpassing the other models tested. The VGG model also showed competitive performance with a slightly higher overall F1-Score of 0.7481, although its precision and recall were less balanced on a class basis than FCNN. The SVM model, although achieving the top classspeciﬁc F1-score for the Sell category at 0.472, performed below overall with an F1-Score of 0.7431 and accuracy of 0.7413, owing to less-than-stellar performance on the Buy and Hold categories. These ﬁndings highlight the strength of MTF-based features encoding in improving model ability to learn temporal dependencies and subtle patterns in ﬁnancial time series. This research shows how combining MTF transformations with deep learning frameworks like FCNN can greatly enhance prediction accuracy and consistency in stock market prediction. Further, to provide a comparative baseline, we cite Chauhan et al. \[ 8 \], who used MTF-based representations to compare some deep learning architectures. They achieved the following F1-scores and accuracies: 0.66 / 0.68 for VGG, 0.60 / 0.60 for ResNet-50, 0.69 / 0.71) for Inception V3, 0.56 / 0.65 for MobileNet V2, and 0.69 / 0.72 for Xception. Our new FCNN model performs better than all the structures previously shown, as indicated in Table 3, showing improved classiﬁcation accuracy and F1-score, which means higher reliability and ﬂexibility in capturing complex temporal-spatial patterns (Table 5 ).

## 5 **Discussion and Limitations **

## The results of the experiment emphasize how the use of Markov Transition Field (MTF)

transformations into a compressed feature space greatly improves the predictive powers of machine learning models in stock price movement classiﬁcation as indicated in Table 4. Of the models tested, the Fully Connected Neural Network (FCNN) proved to be the strongest and well-balanced, producing better results both in accuracy and overall F1-score "Fig. 5 ". This indicates that FCNNs, when combined with MTF representations, are able to successfully extract the non-linear temporal dependencies typical of ﬁnancial time series data. The VGG model, while initially intended for image processing, also beneﬁted from the MTF input with competitive overall F1 performance; however, it was class-imbalanced in its favorability towards SELL class predictions. Conversely, the SVM model demonstrated localized power in capturing SELL signals but no balance across classes, most probably owing to its poor ability to capture intricate, non-linear relationships in high-dimensional compressed spaces.

## Despite encouraging ﬁndings, the current research has a number of limitations. The

data were constrained, hindering generalizability across different ﬁnancial instruments and trading conditions. MTF supports temporal relationships compactly, yet effectiveness is bound to hard-coded quantization values and compression rates, not optimized. Class imbalance could have biased model performance, especially for SVMs, with lower representational capacity. The lack of ensemble methods and hyperparameter tuning limits performance benchmarking. As much as FCNNs were effective, more advanced models such as Transformers or hybrid attention-based models could be analyzed in the future to enhance forecasting accuracy and explainability. Yet, through enhanced market awareness and the promotion of correct decision-making, the model may be useful for investors as individuals. It also promotes broader availability in ﬁnancial analytics because of the conversion to low-cost computing hardware. V.K. Pandey et al.

## 6 **Conclusion **

## This study demonstrates that integrating Markov Transition Field transformations with

compressed feature spaces signiﬁcantly boosts the classiﬁcation performance of stock market models. The FCNN model, when integrated with MTF, achieves superior accuracy and balanced performance across all labels Buy, Hold, and Sell positioning it as a reliable model for ﬁnancial forecasting tasks mentioned in "Fig. 5 ". Although the VGG and SVM models show promise in speciﬁc classes, they fall short in maintaining consistent overall performance. The ﬁndings underscore the importance of temporal encoding and appropriate feature compression in handling complex ﬁnancial time series by achieving 74% accuracy. While there is room for further exploration and improvement, especially in terms of generalization and hyperparameter tuning, the current approach sets a strong foundation for developing efﬁcient and accurate predictive models in algorithmic trading and ﬁnancial analytics.
