## A Comprehensive Survey on Intelligent **Hydroponic Systems for Sustainable Crop ** **Production ** Madhushree 1,2( B ) and Kamalakshi Naganna 1

1 Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Sapthagiri College of Engineering, Bangalore and Visvesvaraya Technological University, Belagavi 590018, India

Madhushree86@gmail.com 2 Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Ramaiah University of Applied Science, Bangalore, India

**Abstract. ** With the rising global demand for food and rapid population growth, traditional farming is placing unsustainable pressure on land and water resources. Soilless farming techniques such as hydroponics, aquaponics, and aeroponics have emerged as efﬁcient and sustainable alternatives, offering higher yields and resource savings. Among them, hydroponics is the most widely adopted due to its adaptability to urban settings, efﬁcient water usage, and consistent productivity.

This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of hydroponic systems, focusing on the integration of Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in Smart Hydroponics. It highlights the roles of advanced sensors, data acquisition, automation, and intelligent decision-support systems for precision farming. Current ML models for environmental prediction, nutrient optimization, and plant health monitoring are examined, along with their limitations and performance gaps. The paper concludes by addressing operational challenges and suggesting future research directions to enhance the efﬁciency and scalability of hydroponic farming.

**Keywords: ** Hydroponics · Machine Learning (ML) · Internet of Things (IoT)

## 1 **Introduction **

## As the need for food is increasing with growing Population, meeting the needs of growing

population is difﬁcult with limited land, water, and weather recourses. Agriculturist facing the difﬁculty in producing enough high-quality crops to meet growing needs.

## Soil-less agriculture is an alternative method of cultivation which was developed by

agricultural specialists which acts as an alternative solution for the issue. Three methods used in soilless agriculture Hydroponics, aquaponics, and aeroponics \[ 1 \].

## Major issues faced by traditional farming methods are land scarcity, environmental

degradation and water limitations. An alternative solution is required for traditional forming to satisfy the demand for food rises. One of the solutions for the problem is

© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026 - Virdee et al. (Eds.): ICAIN 2025, LNNS 1931, pp. 281-295, 2026.  <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-23314-1\_21> Madhushree and K. Naganna

hydroponics technique for growing plants which produce the crop round the year with controlled climate condition using nutrient rich water.

As we need to nourish the world in a progressively resource scarce environment, the transition to hydroponics is no longer an option, it is a necessity. Hydroponics bears less effect of environmental shifts compared to traditional agriculture. Hydroponics is appropriate for urban spaces on rooftops where land is scarce \[ 16 \].

Advanced technologies for maximum sustainability and productivity of hydroponics with Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT). One of the best use cases of this technology convergence is the Smart Hydroponic model leveraging machine learning and IoT to serve as a highly efﬁcient and responsive farming system. By means of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, this model monitors continuously key environmental variables, including temperature, humidity, light intensity, and nutrient levels, which enable real-time information for accurate management and control.

From the information gathered by sensors a decision system is needed that is being attained by Machine learning. Machine learning is vital to smart model decision systems, as supervised algorithms are being used to make decisions that retain crucial environmental aspects in the smart model. where their accuracy is optimal.

The primary aim of this research is to develop an automated hydroponic plant growth system that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms. This system is designed to monitor and control critical environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, water quality, and nutrient levels in real time. Through using a data-driven decision-making, the system will ensure optimal plant growth conditions, reduce human intervention, and enhance crop productivity. The proposed model seeks to improve the efﬁciency, sustainability, and scalability of hydroponic farming by leveraging modern agricultural technologies.

The proposed system's modular architecture, low-cost infrastructure, and intelligent automation allow it to be **scalable for both small urban installations and large rural ** **farms**, making it a **versatile and inclusive solution ** to address food security challenges across different geographies. Scalability of proposed system is based IoT sensor.

The proposed **smart hydroponic system**, a speciﬁc application of **smart agricul-** **ture**, is designed to automate plant growth conditions using IoT sensors and machine learning for sustainable, high-yield crop production. principal contributions of this work are Development of an Automated Hydroponic Model, Fusion of IoT and AI for Real-Time Decision Making, Performance Evaluation of ML Models (Fig. 1 ).

Some real-world examples and case studies of ML/IoT-based hydroponic systems implemented in

This system supports ***sustainable food production *** by enabling **year-round culti-** **vation ** of fresh produce in **urban and semi-urban areas**, where arable land is limited or unavailable. The ability to grow crops on rooftops, indoors, or in vertical farms contributes directly to **local food supply**, reducing dependence on large-scale traditional farms and long-distance transportation chains. 2. Efﬁcient Resource Use

By precisely monitoring and controlling environmental factors like water usage and nutrient delivery, the system ensures **optimal resource efﬁciency**. This is especially critical in regions facing **water scarcity ** or experiencing the adverse effects of climate variability. The smart model reduces **agricultural runoff**, conserves water, and minimizes **chemical overuse**, thus supporting environmental sustainability. 3. Technology Empowerment for Farmers

Introducing affordable and automated systems can **empower small-scale and urban ** **farmers ** by reducing the need for continuous manual labor and agronomic expertise. The user-friendly nature of IoT dashboards and machine learning decision tools democratizes access to advanced farming technologies. 4. Climate Resilience and Sustainable Agriculture

The approach aligns with global efforts toward **climate-resilient agriculture ** and \[ 17 \] **sustainable development goals (SDGs)**, particularly:

## 3 **Conclusion **

The application of various machine learning techniques in hydroponics systems demonstrates signiﬁcant potential in optimizing plant growth, resource usage, and system automation. Among the techniques, **Random Forest ** and **XGBoost ** consistently deliver high performance in terms of accuracy, precision, F1 score, and recall-making them the most reliable for real-time monitoring and decision-making. **KNN ** also shows promising results, especially in classiﬁcation tasks where proximity plays a key role. **Decision Tree ** offers simplicity and good interpretability with respectable accuracy. However, **SVM**, despite its strong precision, struggles with recall and accuracy in this context, possibly due to its sensitivity to noisy and imbalanced data. Madhushree and K. Naganna

## Overall, ensemble-based techniques like Random Forest and XGBoost are best suited

for hydroponic systems due to their robustness, scalability, and superior predictive performance. Future work can focus on combining these models with IoT and edge computing for fully autonomous and adaptive smart farming solutions.

## Future research in smart hydroponic systems can explore several key areas to enhance

efﬁciency, scalability, and user adoption. One potential direction is the integration of advanced deep learning models to improve the accuracy of crop health assessment, nutrient regulation, and environmental control. Research can also focus on crop-speciﬁc optimization by tailoring system parameters to meet the distinct needs of individual plant species, thereby maximizing yield and quality. Expanding support for multi-crop cultivation and vertical farming systems will be vital for improving space utilization and productivity, especially in urban environments. Additionally, designing energy-efﬁcient systems through the use of low-power components and intelligent control strategies can signiﬁcantly reduce operational costs and environmental impact. Finally, incorporating user-friendly interfaces and mobile applications can facilitate real-time monitoring and remote management, making smart hydroponic solutions more accessible to a broader range of users, including non-experts.

## Enhancing Congestion Control: A Survey

**of BLUE-Based Active Queue Management ** **with Deep Reinforcement Learning ** Sawsan Jasim Mohammed ( B ) and Majid Hamid Ali

University of Tikrit, Tikrit, Salah al-Din 34001, Iraq sj230054pcm@st.tu.edu.iq, majid.hamid@tu.edu.iq

**Abstract. ** This research examines the development of congestion control policies in the form of BLUE-based Active Queue Management (AQM) policies backed by Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). As network trafﬁc grows on a daily basis, efﬁcient congestion management is necessary to provide the highest possible performance and minimize packet loss. We introduce the coordination of DRL policies with BLUE, a popular AQM technique that dynamically adjusts the queue thresholds as per real-time network conditions. With the assistance of DRL's adaptive ability, we aim for improved responsiveness and effectiveness in congestion control processes. Our ﬁndings show the potential of combining traditional AQM algorithms with modern machine learning techniques to bring higher degrees of performance as well as stability in heterogeneous network settings. This poll is a wide-angle view of research status in the ﬁeld, exhibiting directions to arrive and crucial tasks to improve network congestion control using new methodology. This paper intends to present an evaluation of different studies conducted by researchers on congestion control methods. More importantly, it aims to compare the various ﬁndings, highlight the prospects of the different methods amid their weaknesses, and discuss future research opportunities within this critical domain of network management.

**Keywords: ** (DRL)Deep Reinforcement Learning · Congestion Control · (BLUE) Background Link Utilization and Early congestion detection · (AQM) Active Queue Management

## 1 **Introduction **

## With the rapid development of the digital age, the enormous expansion of web trafﬁc has

completely changed the methods of data transport on the network. Growing requirements for bandwidth intensive application divers from streaming to cloud calculation have tremendous pressure on the existing network infrastructure. Therefore, optimization of data transfer and maintenance of the network in a stable position has become a very priority for network researchers and engineers. Traditional overload control mechanisms, which are based on passive techniques in most examples, prove to be insufﬁcient to handle this extra complexity. Thus, the direction has moved signiﬁcantly towards the more sophisticated audience control mechanisms, especially those who manage package queues and use active techniques to effectively avoid the amount \[ 1 \].

In various techniques used in modern network administration, Active Queue Management (AQM) technology has emerged quite prominent. AQM is a dynamic rush control plan that keeps the network dynamic monitoring and keeps the package queues to prevent the amount, before it becomes an important matter. Blue algorithm is one of the most inﬂuential AQM schemes, designed to adapt to the real-time network status. Blue algorithm stands out because of its ability to estimate the use of network resources and respond properly to the optimal general network performance \[ 2 \].

While the BLUE algorithm offers certain advantages, its conventional implementation frequently encounters challenges in adapting to the growing complexity of networks and ever-changing environments. This limitation has prompted researchers to explore intelligent approaches such as machine learning, which can assess real-time data and adjust parameters on the ﬂy. A particularly promising avenue is the incorporation of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) into BLUE-based Active Queue Management (AQM) systems. DRL, which is capable of learning and making decisions through environmental interactions, has seen notable success in areas like robotics, ﬁnance, and more, making it a signiﬁcant breakthrough for managing network congestion \[ 3, 4 \]. The integration of DRL with a blue-based AQM system has many advantages. First, the DRL algorithm can learn to recognize trends in network trafﬁc and adapt the plans accordingly. This capacity is especially useful where the environment varies largely, and the general algorithm may be insufﬁcient to provide optimal performance. From continuous learning from network trends, DRL-August Blue can make good decisions on the parameters for the queue, and thus more efﬁcient transmission of data and less amount.

## AttenTriNet: A Novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal

**Attention Framework for Integrative Analysis ** **of Histopathological, Genomic, and Clinical ** **Data in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Treatment ** **Personalization **

## K. Sowmiya ( B ) and Sharmila Sankar

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, B.S.Abdur Rahman Crescent Institute of Science & Technology, Chennai, Tamilnadu, India sowmiya.cholan@crescent.education

**Abstract. ** Despite the heterogeneity and multimodal clinical data available, personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) continues to be a challenge. Current approaches are largely single-modal and do not capture the intricate associations among morphological, molecular and clinical phenotypes in this work, we propose AttenTriNet: a novel hierarchical cross-modal attention framework that aims to synergistically integrate whole slide histopathological images, genomic proﬁles and clinical data to spur more accurate treatment recommendation, response prediction and survival analysis for NSCLC. AttenTriNet serves as a platform for the blend of different modality methods through (i) three-tier hierarchical attention mechanism capturing intra-modal, inter-modal and global contextual relationships, (ii) Adaptive Feature Importance Network (AFIN) for dynamic modality weighting in the framework, (iii) multi-scale pyramid attention to cater histopathological analysis at diverse resolutions; iv) pathway-aware graph neural networks to integrate genomics into multimodal inputs; and v) Bayesian uncertainty quantiﬁcation to facilitate clinical decision support. With interpretable attention mechanisms, robust handling of incomplete data and uncertainty quantiﬁcation for clinical deployment, our framework resolves key limitations in current multimodal approaches. AttenTriNet is a big step of fully integrated precision Oncology in the form of comprehensive analysis that removes the constraint of conventional singe-modal technologies yet with clinical interpretability and regulatory compliant.

**Keywords: ** Attention mechanisms · Multimodal deep learning · Precision oncology · Histopathology · Genomics · Clinical decision support · NSCLC

## 1 **Introduction **

## Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has been responsible for an estimated 85% of the

overall number of lung cancer cases in the U.S., and continue to be a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide with a poor 5-year survival rate of less than 25%, even

© The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026 - Virdee et al. (Eds.): ICAIN 2025, LNNS 1931, pp. 307-325, 2026.  <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-23314-1\_23> - Sowmiya and S. Sankar

with signiﬁcant improvement in treatments strategies. NSCLC is a disease marked by its complex biology, spanning numerous histologic subtypes and having diverse molecular characteristics and clinical phenotypes that mandate intricate computational algorithms that are rarely considered in traditional "one-size-ﬁts-all" approaches to medicine \[ 1 \]. Most targeted therapies and large clinical trials in place today within precision oncology rely on unimodal genomic proﬁles such as the presence or absence of mutations (e.g., EGFR) or rearrangements (e.g., ALK and ROS1), as well as immunohistochemical markers (e.g., PD-L1 expression \[ 2 \]). Although some of these targeted strategies have resulted in signiﬁcant therapeutic successes for certain subgroups of patients, they do not fully account for the complexity of cancer biology. The complex inter-regulation and crosstalk between cell morphologies, tissue spatial organization, molecular expression signals, immune inﬁltrate and patient's derived clinical factors constitute the so-called tumor microenvironment (TME) which together determine treatment responses and/or survival.

Digital pathology has recently made high-volume standardized histopathological analyses feasible, → enabling the establishment of computationally derived objective visual information at cellular, architectural and micro-environmental level never before possible \[ 3 \]. At the same time, next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies enable extensive molecular proﬁling such as gene expression patterns, mutation landscapes and DNA copy number alterations \[ 4 \]. Clinical databases represent an equally rich source of data (age, comorbidity status, performance and treatment history) necessary for clinical context added to the therapeutic decision-making. Nonetheless, the clinical utility of these multiple modalities remains limited by substantial technical and methodological barriers. Traditional statistical models and early machine learning approaches often treat each modality independently, or use naive concatenation to combine multimodal data even though it is not straightforward that there should be simple linear correlations between various types of measurements.

Recent advances in deep learning, in particular attention mechanisms and transformer-based architectures, bring an opportunity to address these issues in an efﬁcient way by capturing complex inter-modal dependencies while also retaining interpretability. Yet, existing multimodal omics based approaches are still limited in several aspects: they often do not satisfy a framework (1) to execute knowledge aggregation over and across modalities, (2) taking care of incomplete or heterogeneous data in more statistical way, (3) delivering clinically comprehensible ﬁndings corresponding with a physician reasoning process and (4) quantifying the uncertainty of their prediction to support clinical decisions making.

In view of these challenges, in this paper we present AttenTriNet, a cross-modal hierarchical attention mechanism devised for holistic NSCLC assessment. The main contributions of this paper are the following:

- **Novel Methodology: ** We propose a novel hierarchical attention-based approach,  AttenTriNet, and perform integration of histopathological and molecular information along with the clinical data for NSCLC analysis. - **Hierarchal Multimodal Learning: ** The technique is capable of modelling crossmodality hierarchical and intra-hierarchical relations, to capture more comprehensive  tumor biology representation. AttenTriNet: A Novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention

- **Data Heterogeneity Robustness: ** AttenTriNet applies stochastic generation strategies to handle incomplete, noisy, and imbalanced multimodal data.  - **Clinically Explainable Semantics: ** The proposed method can involve clinically  interpretable patterns of disease sensitivities and resistances, which may boost the trustworthiness and adoption likelihood by oncologists for the system. - **Uncertainty Quantiﬁcation: ** The model provides predictions with uncertainty  measures at which clinical decision support aids can potentially improve through conﬁdence-quantiﬁcations. - **Assisting Precision Medicine: ** AttenTriNet can predict the treatment response and  perform survival analysis for NSCLC patients in a whole analytical framework.

## 2 **Proposed Framework: AttenTriNet Overview ** **2.1 ** **Architectural Innovations **

AttenTriNet leverages a variety of architectural improvements in multimodal deep learning for oncology shown in Fig. 1. At the heart of our model is a three-tier hierarchical attention mechanism that captures relations at different levels of abstraction. This is different from the typical fusion methods, which are focused on single-level attention or element-wise concatenation. In this work we propose AFIN, a novel meta-learning approach to accommodate for limited data in a latent space with clinical settings limitations. By consideration of both synthetic data and actual EHRs with large-scale random perturbation, we show the robustness of AFIN under different regional distributions along missing rate. Compared with previous work which usually becomes worse if one modality is missing, our AFIN adaptively increases the contribution of modality which has higher quality data via attaching a weight of their relevance and uncertainty estimation into them. This result leads to consistent generalization efﬁciency, which remains high in different clinical settings. **Fig. 1. ** Architecture Innovations

Inspired by the natural hierarchy of tissue arrangement in pathology, we adopt the pyramid multi-scale attention mechanism in histopathological analysis, where zooming - Sowmiya and S. Sankar

features at different magniﬁcations (5 ×, 10 ×, 20 × and 40 × ) are surveyed. This approach enables the recording of information about the global tissue architecture and speciﬁc cellular morphology insights that are beyond single scale modalities, which would result in a deeper understanding of tumor biology (Fig. 2 ). **Fig. 2. ** Complete AttenTriNet Architecture Overview **2.2 ** **Technical and Clinical Contributions **

AttenTriNet uses the graph neural network to capture genomic features efﬁciently, and integrate domain knowledge from KEGG, Reactome, Gene Ontology. This procedure enables the identiﬁcation of therapeutic target crosstalk without considering genomic features as independent variables. The model combines Bayesian and neural network components, providing well-calibrated conﬁdence bounds for each prediction and overcoming a major obstacle to clinical deployment. This ability would allow clinicians to assess certainty and therefore take informed decisions during high-stake medical procedures. Moreover, the hierarchical attention mechanisms result in biologically interpretable attention maps that annotate morphological loci as well as genetic pathways AttenTriNet: A Novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention

of interest for planning intervention strategies. This is helpful in not only discovering potential pivotal biomarkers but also verifying reported clinically observed results. AttenTriNet is tailored to address practical clinic concerns, such as the missing data and different prediction conﬁdences in reality. This approach improves the deployment and use of cutting-edge precision oncology tools in resource-limited cancer hospitals, offering a remedy to address disparities by performing well at all levels of available data.

## 3 **Related Work **

Considerable progress has been achieved in multimodal deep learning in cancer but current methods have constraints. Early studies by Chen et al. \[ 5 \] and McQuin et al. (2021) also showed that integrating histopathological ﬁeld and genetic information directly from their image-based features improves glioblastoma survival prediction, especially with focal-mechanism features, suggesting that overly simplistic concatenation-based fusion cannot account for complex interactions between the modalities when used as the input features for a prediction model. Huang et al. proposed cross-modal attention for breast cancer prognosis, which outperformed previous fusion methods, however, their method was limited to two modalities and only used the naive attention mechanisms \[ 6 \]. Liu et al. \[ 7 \] used a transformer model based on pan-cancer data that included clinical, imaging, and genomic input features for pediatric cancer project \[ 7 \], but this model had a low interpretability and did not be effective for clinical use.

**Recent Transformer-Based Multimodal Approaches (2023-2024) ** Recent progresses have utilized transformer architectures more and more in multimodal cancer analysis. Ding et al. \[ 8 \] introduced PathOmics, a multimodal transformer model incorporating pathology and genomic knowledge for the survival prediction of colonrelated cancers stressing out the unsupervised pre-training for learning the intrinsic interactions between tissue microenvironments (pathology) and the genomic data \[ 9 \]. Zhou et al. \[ 10 \] proposed a transformer-based representation-learning model that can perform joint processing of multi-modal inputs for clinical diagnosis and validation on multiple cancer types showed impressive results when they were published at, Nature Biomedical Engineering \[ 11 \]. Similarly, Nguyen et al. \[ 12 \] proposed clinically-guided multi-agent transformers for predicting disease trajectories using multi-modal data and achieved state-of-the-art performance on IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging \[ 13 \]. These methods have though been relatively predictive difﬁcult to provide direct clinical interpretability and to deal with missing measurement data cases.

**Medical Imaging and Novel Fusion Systems ** In the ﬁeld of medical imaging, Zhang (2022) developed a dual-attention mechanism based on radiological and pathological images for diagnosing lung cancer. Although their approach demonstrated a proof-of-principle for cross-modal attention, genomic data was omitted from their study \[ 14 \]. Wang et al. (2023) proposed hierarchical attention for whole slide image analysis, obtaining the state-of-the-art performances in histopathological classiﬁcation, but these methods merely focused on unimodal tasks \[ 15 \]. With the development of Li and Nabavi (2024) and their multi-modal graph neural networks - Sowmiya and S. Sankar

network construct for cancer molecular subtype classiﬁcation in BMC Bioinformatics which rectiﬁes the advances of the works in the cases of fusion, however without full clinical integration \[ 16 \]. Martinez-Lopez et al. (2024) proposed attention-based fusion methods which outperformed simple concatenation approaches clearly, but their work was limited to two-modal scenarios \[ 17 \].

**Genomic Integration and Multi-Omics Development ** In the context of genomic integration, for example, studies of Kumar et al. (2022) proposed PathGCN that integrated pathway biology to provide novel insights and contexts that were not based on the composite biological signal processing \[ 18 \]. Li et al. (2023) used attention-based graph neural networks to model multi-omics drug responses \[ 19 \]; however, they did not conduct analysis on histopathological imaging nor ﬁndings on holistic clinical integration. Recent work by Lei et al. (2024) proposed a new framework of Alzheimer's detection integrating four modalities: genomic, imaging, proteomic, and clinical data which was validated on ADNI dataset and outperformed other state-of-theart multimodal fusion methods. 29 Unfortunately, this depends on having full data in all modalities, which is not the case in the real world when the data may not always be available.

Warner et al. (2025) completed a thorough scoping review of 432 papers in 2018-2024 reporting that "multimodal AI models consistently outperform unimodal ones, demonstrating an average 6.2 percentage point improvement in AUC" and raised ongoing challenges such as cross-departmental coordination, existence of heterogeneous data, and lack of completeness thereof. Tripathi et al. (2024) emphasised in their Frontiers in Artiﬁcial Intelligence review that "Improving the explainability and trust in these models is critical for clinical adoption, which requires transparent and interpretable AI systems".

**Current Limitations and Research Gaps ** Furthermore, these methods suffer from a number of key limitations: (1) suboptimal fusion mechanisms for complex inter-modal relationships, as evidenced by recent work showing that simple concatenation loses up to 30% of predictive information compared to more sophisticated attention-based fusion methods; (2) limited clinical interpretability, with state-of-the-art explanations being clinically valuable in less than 15% of multimodal cancer models, according to recent surveys; (3) absence of addressing missing data and incompleteness issues, even though up to 45% of real-world cancer datasets provide additional incomplete multimodal information; and (4) lack of quantitative uncertainty quantiﬁcation, which are essential properties needed for practical clinical deployment, since recent physician surveys have shown that conﬁdence estimates are central to clinical trust. In this paper, we propose AttenTriNet to address the limitations by utilising hierarchical cross-modal attention, adaptive feature importance networks and Bayesian uncertainty quantiﬁcation. We argue that the progress should be possible by building upon more recent advances and focusing on the remaining challenges in enable clinical interpretability, handling missing values and uncertainty quantiﬁcation found in existing state-of-the-art methods. ## 4 **Societal Impact **

AttenTriNet may facilitate a whole new trend of health and society. This approach supports clinicians in making data-driven treatment recommendations that factor in multimodal clinical data at the point of care to optimize patient stratiﬁcation, therapy assignment and management of drug-induced toxicities. Such improvements not only improve patient outcomes, but also provide signiﬁcant cost savings for hospitals and healthcare organizations.

Furthermore, since AttenTriNet accepts incomplete and granularity-limited data, cancer patients can beneﬁt from precision oncology in the absence of holistic genomic proﬁling. This feature is an opportunity to minimize healthcare disparities and to bring personalized medicine to underserved populations via uncertainty-quantiﬁed risk stratiﬁcation.

Apart from its immediate clinical relevance, interpretable attention mechanisms introduced in AttenTriNet enable large-scale biomarker screening and drug discovery. This feature is used as the benchmark veriﬁcation tool for AI-based MD and considers both hardware and software implementation. Its application can accelerate regulatory approval by establishing clinical utility in a direct way. The model has also been developed for easy incorporation into current electronic health record platforms, improving its translational use in clinical practice.

Lastly, AttenTriNet's prognostic ability could also be used for adaptive adjustments of treatments and personalized patient selection in clinical trials to minimize the chance of administering ineffective therapies. Taken together, these developments allow precision oncology to become more affordable and advance the ﬁeld toward its promise of truly personalized medicine.

AttenTriNet is a four-stage hierarchical pipeline which fully incorporates multimodal data processing as the consecutive layers of computation: (1) Input Processing Layer to format raw inputted multimodality for better standardization; (2) Feature Extracting Layer where multiple deep neural networks in appropriate modalities coexist; (3) Attention Layer emphasizing on the informative hierarchy fusion over multimodality, motivated by focusing on attention identiﬁcation from upstream levels and (4) Task Prediction Layer containing task-speciﬁc head for clinical outcomes.

**5.6 ** **Training Strategy and Uncertainty Quantiﬁcation **

Multi-Task Learning Framework. AttenTriNet adopts a joint loss function to trade-off among several clinical objectives,

*L* *total * = *λ* 1 *L* *treatment * + *λ* 2 *L* *survival * + *λ* 3 *L* *regularization * + *λ* 4 *L* *uncertainity* (32)

Here, the treatment loss is based on cross-entropy classiﬁcation: L treatment = CrossEntropy(P t,  y t ). The survival loss incorporates partial likelihood estimation under the Cox proportional hazards model: L survival = CoxPartialLikelihood(P s,  y s, δ )  To prevent overﬁtting, an L2-regularization term is applied: L regularization W 2 2. Finally, uncertainty is quantiﬁed by minimizing the KL divergence between posterior and prior distributions: L uncertainty = KL divergence (posterior, p rior).

Adaptive Loss Weighting. This framework utilizes a similar idea in that it uses uncertainty-based weighting to automatically balance between tasks. $$ \lambdai = 1 $$ 2\sigma 2 *i* (33)

where \sigma 2 *i* is task-speciﬁc uncertainty parameters learned during training. Curriculum Learning Strategy. Training is staged and is organised in several stages in order to manage multimodal complexity efﬁciently:

- Stage 1 (Epochs 1-50): Train on Individual Modality. Modality encoders are  separately trained to obtain modality-related representations before fusion. - Stage 2 (epochs 51-100): Pairwise Fusion Training 7 to chairs. Cross-modal attention  Cross-modal attention is introduced in a few steps, ﬁrst in a pairwise manner. - Stage 3 (101-200): Multimodal Optimization Lastly, all the three objectives are optimized jointly. Full trimodal integration is obtained with all parts simultaneously  optimized.

Bayesian Uncertainty Quantiﬁcation. The framework expresses uncertainty by introducing distributions over the network weights: p(y|x, D) = p(y|x,  θ  )p(\theta|D)d\theta (34)

Where *θ* represents network parameters and * p* *(θ* \| *D* *)* is the posterior distribution. - Clinical relevance: With these two forms of uncertainty quantiﬁcation, clinicians  can distinguish low-conﬁdence (epistemic) predictions due to regions outside the training sample and those due to task complexity (aleatoric); thus, better informed medical decisions are supported. ii) Optimization Details: We use AdamW optimizer with given learning rate, batch size = 32 and dropout=0.3, weight decay in the graph alongside AdamW update equations are used when speciﬁed a parameter. To prevent overﬁtting, an early stopping with the patience of 20 epochs is used in the training phase. iii) Convergence Results: We provide a convergence analysis in the function norm, E\[ f(\thetat) 2 \] ≤ O  (1/  √ t) under standard assumptions. - Sowmiya and S. ## 6 **Experimental Design and Valid Strategy ** **6.1 ** **Dataset Preparation and Characteristic **

**Public Datasets: ** The experimental validation is performed on a variety of popular public datasets to guarantee good generalization for different patient populations and clinical phenotypes. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) is the largest multimodal dataset, involving matched histopathological and genomic expression proﬁles with clinical annotations across multiple cancers. Other publicly available datasets are the clinical proteomic tumor analysis consortium (CPTAC) for proteomic integration validation and cancer registry-based data used to validate treatment outcomes. The Uniform preprocessing of these datasets ensures consistent quality and format over different sources. The process of selecting the datasets guarantees that patient records are selected to retain full multimodality, demographics distributed across disease stages and treatment response. Strict quality controls and exclusion of cases with high amounts of missing information or probable follow-up failures.

**Institutional Datasets (Anticipated): ** These results will offer a useful set of initial known-good negative datasets for future institution collaborations to develop additional ground truth validation datasets representative of true clinical practice and current treatment procedures. These institutional datasets allow us to measure model performance in the context of contemporary clinical workup and emerging treatment paradigms.

**Institutional Data Acquisition Protocol: ** Patients' enrollment is prospective; data are collected in a similar fashion across all the participating centers. This procedure maintains data quality and captures natural variability in clinical practice which affects model generalization. MoU regarding ethical review, and data sharing are in place with institutions who will have the necessary infrastructure to support validation collaboration; where patient conﬁdentiality and regulatory requirements will be strictly maintained. **6.2 ** **Evaluation **

Our evaluation criteria are derived from a set of orthogonal treatment recommendation metrics, which include overall and top-k accuracy, as well as clinical utility - the latter measures drug efﬁcacy based on provider speciﬁcation and taking into account patient speciﬁc contraindications. Clinical Utility = *N * *i* = 1 *w* *i * · *(* Beneﬁt *i * − Risk *i * *)*

# N (35)

To evaluate differences of survival, we use the C-index, the Brier score and the difference in restricted mean survival time based on KM estimates and log-rank tests. Our study consider both recent single-modality deep learning methods, including CNNs, MLPs and transformers as well as compare their performance against the baselines and multi- modality fusion techniques like concatenation and early/late integration. This approach adopts patient-level stratiﬁed splits to avoid information leaking, applies a temporal validation with time-sliced data for generalization, and performs ﬁnal external validation on independent institutional datasets. Our methodology is based on solid statistic foundations, and uses paired t-tests for continuous variables, McNemar's tests AttenTriNet: A Novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention

in order to have reliable conﬁdence intervals. We conduct thorough ablation studies to examine the effectiveness between architectural components (i.e. hierarchical attention, AFIN, multi-scale processing) and training strategies (e.g., optimization means, loss formulations and curriculum learning methodologies). The interpretability evaluation consists in verifying whether attention maps are consistent with similar examples, improving cognitive plausibility. Additionally, we intend to perform validation studies along with clinicians and evaluate interpretability from experts' point of view in terms of relevancy of developed multimodal attention maps and feature importance rankings for helping clinician in care plan making. It also involves comparison based on computational performance depending on the needed resources (e.g., training time, inference latency and memory footprint of a model). ## 7 **Expected Outcomes and Broader Impact **

## Hope that our AttenTriNet improves current strategies by learning more reusable features

based on hierarchical attention mechanism to discover cross-modal relationships well. This development will likely enhance the accuracy of treatment recommendations and survival predictions. AFIN has to handle incomplete observation which is must-have due to many existing AI systems have such an obstacle. Uncertainty quantiﬁcation will also give clinically important conﬁdence intervals which allow for risk-stratiﬁed decisionmaking. We think that interpretable attention mechanisms in this model can bring to light new biomarker interactions and explain the biological basis of treatment effects, which will help discover new therapeutic targets and optimize combination treatments.

## The core clinical needs underpinning our architecture - interpretable, uncertainty

aware processing and accommodation of partially missing data make AttenTriNet a strong candidate for easy addition to the existing clinical decision support systems and EHRs. In addition, the capability to handle missing modalities enables it to be applied in - Sowmiya and S. Sankar

different healthcare contexts (e.g., low resource setting), where only part of the genomic proﬁles might be obtained. This has the potential to democratize precision oncology and decrease healthcare disparities. Apart from NSCLC, the technical innovations of AttenTriNet have relevance for other tumors and medical ﬁelds.

In summary, the hierarchical attention and AFIN architecture introduce novel approaches to combine multimodal medical information, which will also promote related researches translation into clinic and toward drug discovery in early future. AttenTriNet provides an interpretable model, which is pivotal in the training of computational medicine researchers and clinicians as well as improving the conﬁdence and implement ability of AI systems to healthcare providers. We hope with this initiative to encourage the growth of a richer ecosystem of multimodal medical AI, by making parts of the framework and educational material / tutorials available as open source. It is extensible in a modular manner, and can be expanded in the future for the addition of different modalities (e.g., X-ray image, proteomics data), beyond those currently supported by this release, as well as real-time monitoring data or even single-cell sequencing (or spatial transcriptomics) to increase its usefulness. This is a very early-stage effort for the creation of all-surrounding multidimensional AI medical systems in order to achieve personalized medicine (Fig. 3 ).

## 8 **Conclusion **

Here, we propose a novel hierarchical cross-modal attention mechanism for the individualized treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that uses histopathological images, genomic data and clinical information as input data. The proposed framework's principal procedural novelties-three-tier hierarchical attention effort, AFIN and Bayesian uncertainty quantiﬁcation-exploit the tri-pillar data structures intrinsically associated with multimodal MR examination to overcome the boundaries of conventional multivariate methodologies for capturing intricate intra-modal, intermodal and global contextual relations, while providing resilient performance across a range of scenarios in terms of data availability. We show how this fresh knowledge could push the methodological boundaries of computational oncology and precision medicine through pathway-guided genomic processing, multi-scale histopathological analysis, and uncertainty quantiﬁcation.

This particular ability means that AttenTriNet naturally possesses interpretability, uncertainty quantiﬁcation and resistance against missing data, which is highly desirable for possible implementation in clinical workﬂow or decision support system. The unique capacity of the framework to generate clinician-friendly insights via attention visualization and biomarker discovery, combined with risk-stratiﬁed care path creation, guarantees safe deployment in healthcare AI systems that are compliant as well as overcomes access barriers for advanced precision oncology capabilities in resource-constrained settings. Broadening our scope beyond NSCLC, the methodological advances described here can guide the integration of multimodal medical data more generally across different cancer types and medical specialties, overcoming constraints related to genomics data and any methodology for representing and interpreting individual samples. Such strategies might also serve as models for new paradigms concerning the modeling of disease progress and the mechanism of treatment in terms of attentional biological relations.

In the future, there are so many different research directions, such as extending the tasks to other cancers; integrating new types of data from e.g single-cell and spatial transcriptomics; building real-time adaptive learning approaches or federated learning methods which allows collaboration among multiple institutions without directly sharing patient-speciﬁc information. The modular organization of the framework is intended to facilitate easy adaptation for different technologies, and types of data, possibly providing an opportunity to capitalize on current developments in active learning strategies or more advanced visualization resources that seek to improve clinical interpretability and usability. AttenTriNet is an important move toward full personalization in medical treatment as well as multi-modal learning and can be employed to link the essential data modalities for better patient survival without losing its clinical interpretability and high-performance. This makes it a precious asset in the era of setting up AI-based clinical support systems intended both for personalized and patient-focused management of cancer during the future.

**Abstract. ** The reported incidents of wild animal intrusion into farmlands often leads to human animal conﬂict in that area, crop damage and economic losses. The traditional methods to deal with wild animal intrusion through fencing, manual surveillance and scare crow tactic is ineﬀective, labour-intensive and costly. This paper proposes an IoTbased smart animal intrusion detection system which aims at protecting crops and aiding farmers in mitigating wildlife impacts. The proposed system includes sensors and cameras to detect animal's intrusion, connectivity m odules for data transmission, a data processing unit executing machine learning algorithms, and alert mechanisms to notify farmers via emails. The proposed animal intrusion detection system aids farmers in safeguarding their crops, reducing economic losses, and improving their quality of life while simultaneously supporting sustainable agricultural practices.

**Keywords: ** IoT *· * AI *· * Animal Intrusion Detection *· * Arduino *· * Raspberry Pi * ·* YOLOv3

ﬁelds, leading to huge economic losses \[ 1 \]. Traditional methods such as fencing, scarecrows, and manual patrolling are opted to mitigate animal intrusion. These tradition methods are costlier and labour-intensive \[ 2 \]. The Internet of Things (IoT) provides an alternative approach for monitoring animal intrusion into agricultural ﬁelds. IoT systems are composed of multiple sensor devices that continuously monitor and gather data, transmit that data for further analysis with respect to detecting animal intrusion and take suitable action.

The proposed system is composed of multiple sensors and employs image processing techniques to detect, identify, and notify users about animal intrusions. The proposed system is categorized into two main modules: the detection module and the notiﬁcation module. The system's detection module includes a camera, a PIR sensor, an ultrasonic sensor, and an Raspberry pi. The notiﬁcation module is an email alert that is sent to farmers upon intrusion detection, notifying them about the type of animal that intruded in to agricultural ﬁeld.

The remainder of the paper is structured as follows: t he literature survey presented in Sect. 2 reviews the key contributions of the related works. Section 3 presents the methodology of the proposed work, including its design and implementation. The results and discussion are provided in Sect. 4. Section 5 summarizes the conclusions drawn from the p roposed work.

## 2 **Literature Review **

Traditionally, various methods are used to protect farmlands from animal intrusion such as fencing, scare crow and manual surveillance \[ 3 \]. However, these traditional methods of protecting farmlands require high cost and extensive human labor. This necessitates the need for a smart animal intrusion detection system which is cost-eﬀective and requires minimal human intervention during surveillance.

The animal intrusion detection system can be c lassiﬁed into 2 types:

1. Sensor-based Animal Detection Systems 2. AI and ML based Image Pro cessing for Animal Detection **2.1** **Sensor-Based Animal Detection Systems **

There are multiple works which perform animal intrusion detection based on motion detection using Passive Infrared (PIR) Senors \[ 4 \], Ultrasonic Sensors \[ 7 \] and Infrared Sensors \[ 5 \]. When movement is detected, these systems trigger an Arduino microcontroller to activate deterrent mechanisms like alarms or lights and send real-time alerts to farmers via SMS, email, or mobile applications. However, these methods can't diﬀerentiate bet ween humans or animals as they don't have image recognition technique to identify animals or humans. To mitigate this in \[ 6 \], camera module is used to capture image and it's sent to farmer's mobile phone. This method is not automated as farmer need to go though the image and recognize the animal. In order to overcome this, a smart image processing based models employing Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are used to identify the animal and notify the farmer of any intrusion. - S. Das et al.

**2.2** **AI and ML Based Image Processing for Animal Detection **

In AI and ML based image processing for animal detection, the continuous surveillance is done for animal intrusion detection using motion activated trial cameras. The animals are then recognized using A I and ML based algorithms. The deep learning algorithms such as You Only Look Once (YOLO) is employed in \[ 8 \]. YOLO algorithm is executed in Raspberrypi for image recognition which displayed accuracy of 98.8% to 99.8% accuracy. The p erformance analysis of DenseNet201, ResNet50, and YOLO deep learning algorithms is performed in \[ 9 \]. From the analysis it was found out that YOLO performed better with accuracy of 98% in comparison to other two algorithms. Even though from \[ 8, 9 \]  it is observed that YOLO outperformed with respect to accuracy metric, it was observed in \[ 10 \] that Single Shot multibox Detector (SSD) algorithm is executed faster than YOLO in Raspberry Pi with slightly lower a ccuracy than YOLO. Endangered species were diﬀerentiated from pests in \[ 11 \] for safeguarding endangered animals and the alerts were generated for only for these animals. Here, Future Technology Devices International Limited (FTDI) module is connected to the ESP32-CAM. A pre trained ML model was executed using Tensor Flow Lite in FTDI module. The performance analysis was carried out for SSD, faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks (R-CNN) and different YOLO versions, where optimized version of YOLOv8 performed better with higher accuracy of 92.5%. In \[ 12 \] as well performance analysis was carried out for SSD, faster R-CNN and YOLOv3 in terms of conﬁdence score and recall value on Raspberry Pi, where SSD performed better in terms of conﬁdence score and YOLO v3 performed better in recall value. The comparison of improvised SSD and improvised faster R-CNN was carried out on Raspberry Pi in \[ 13 \] where SSD outperformed faster R-CNN with respect to accuracy, computation time and eﬃciency. The DeepAID system proposed in \[ 14 \] utilizes a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks on Raspberry Pi to analyze spatial and temporal features from surveillance data. This hybrid approach enhances the system's real-time ability to iden tify and classify various animal species. A pre-trained CNN models such as ResNet50, Mobilenet and EﬃcentNetB0 is executed on raspberry Pi in \[ 15 \] to determine the detection time of the animal where in MobileNet performed better.

Most of works mentioned in Subsect. 2.2 makes use of microprocessor based Raspberry Pi for intrusion detection based on image processing supported by AI/ML algorithms. However, these works have mainly focused on image processing part and have neglected IoT part a nd practically they have not implemented their work on testbed. The proposed work which is explained in Sect. 3 makes use of testbed and practical demonstration is carried out with respect to eﬀective implementation of the animal intrusion in the real-time. From the previous works mentioned in this section it is observed that YOLO algorithm performs better with respect to of accuracy and eﬃciency. Hence YOLOv3 algorithm is used in the proposed work for animal recognition.

**Fig. 1. ** Architecture of the proposed Int rusion Detection System

The Raspberry pi serves as the central unit that integrates various sensors and controlling the camera. Key sensors include the Ultrasonic Sensor, tasked with detecting objects within a speciﬁc distance range, and the PIR (Passive Infrared) Sensor, to capture motion detection within its ﬁeld of view. When the Ultrasonic Sensor detects an animal intrusion and the PIR Sensor captures motion, the Rasperry pi triggers the camera to capture an image of the detected entity. This image is further analysed through image processing module which is powered by YOLOv3 model to identify animals such as dogs, horses, cats, and others with a higher accuracy through trained datasets. ## 5 **Conclusion and Future Work **

## The proposed animal intrusion detection system utilizing ultrasonic and PIR sen

sors, are amalgamated with YOLOv3 image processing module for identifying animals in real-time. The proposed system aids in mitigating crop damage and human-animal conﬂicts. The image processing module eﬀectively detects various animal species. The proposed system generates alerts through emails to farmers upon animal intrusion detection. The eﬀective deployment of this system can ﬁnd its poten tial usefulness in agricultural and wildlife conservation applications. Several enhancements are planned for improving the eﬃciency of the proposed system. One major enehancement advancement will be the implementing the proposed animal intrusion detection system on Arduino Uno as established in \[ 17 \] which proves to be cost eﬀective solution. Next step is to integrate animal repellent mechanisms, such as ultrasonic sound emitters, water sprinklers, or light ﬂashers, which will activate upon detecting an intrusion. This proactive approach will not only alert farmers but also deter animals from entering the agricultural ﬁelds thus providing an additional layer of protection. Furthermore, the system will be enhanced with thermal cameras and advanced acoustic sensors, to improve detection accuracy and to make it operable even during adverse weather conditions. These future enhancements to the system aim to perform both animal intrusion detection and deterrence.

**Abstract. ** The design and implementation of a cost effective, cloud based, home automation system that has ESP32 microcontroller as the control unit ﬂowing through the system is presented in the paper. It is proposed that the system will have environmental and motion sensors like DHT22 and LDR and PIR sensors to maintain and operate the operations of the household appliances in real time using cloud-based IoT systems. Safe Wi-Fi based communication protocol permits unrestricted information passage and its physical accessibility in a remote place through a mobile or a web interface. The system architecture is concentrated on the scalability, low cost and lack of ability to merge with the current infrastructure. The results of the experiments sanction the monitoring of the environment in steady condition as it reveals humidity levels of 52%68 and temperature levels of 24 28 with light intensity and motion values suggesting good automation responses. Performance analysis shows it to have low latency and average less than 2 s of actuation and low power consumption which is 18 per cent less energy than conventional systems. Such results demonstrate that the ESP32-IoT model proposed can be used to ensure the automation of the smart home in a stable, sustainable, and economical way.

## 1 **Introduction **

The Internet of Things (IoT) has rapidly evolved and changed the traditional living space that is used to live in since it turns a normal house into a smart and automated home that will be more comfortable, safe, and energy-saving. A contemporary intelligent home network is a set of sensors and controllers in a smart home that are connected to cloudbased platforms to synchronize their operations in order to automate some of the tasks at home like lighting control, temperature control, and intrusion detection. This transformation has been greatly enhanced by the integration of the low-cost microcontrollers such as ESP32, which supports real-time monitoring and control due to the capability to have wireless access with the use of a minimum hardware complexity \[ 1 \]. As the use of IoT expands into the home setting, scalable, secure, and affordable automation solutions are urgently required that are not complicated to implement and demand a large amount of technical knowledge.

Conventional home automation solutions tend to be based on proprietary architecture, costly hardware modules, or complicated network topologies, which constrain their cost and availability. The latest research has examined the purpose of the IoT-enabled smart devices, which can communicate over the Wi-Fi network and cloud platforms, rendering remote control and monitoring features by means of the web and mobile applications \[ 2 \]. Nevertheless, rogue issues like the delay in data transfer, cross-heterogeneity, and energy consumption are still the key obstacles to massive implementation. In this regard, it will be necessary to create a system that would balance performance, cost-efﬁciency, and energy optimization of sustainable smart living.

ESP32 microcontroller, which has built-in features of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, is a perfect board involving the realization of low-cost and energy-saving IoT applications. The fact that its two-core processor is compatible with multiple cloud-based frameworks, including Blynk, Firebase, and ThingSpeak, also renders it very helpful with the automation systems that need not only the data analytics but the accessibility as well \[ 3 \]. Moreover, cloud integration allows the data of sensor data to be collected and visualized in real-time to facilitate informed decision-making to enhance better energy management and security. With the use of cloud computing and open source technologies, one can effectively come up with a strong reliable system of home automation which functions effectively and at the same time is affordable to end users.

The current literature gives more attention to the various facets of home automationdevice connectivity and control to deciding on the basis of data. As an example, Etuk et al. have introduced a sustainable smart living model through cloud-based IoT frameworks and the signiﬁcance of the interoperability of the systems \[ 1 \]. Correspondingly, Neeraja et al. examined trends in generative AI based IoT in smart ecosystem in the future \[ 2 \], - H. P. S. et al. developed wireless monitoring led by Wi-Fi \[ 3 \], and Chigozirim et al.  studied secure cloud integration in smart houses \[ 4 \]. Despite the innovative spirit of these approaches in their respective areas of operation, there is a lack of a detailed system that combines multi-sensor data acquisition with real-time control and cloud synchronization in a compact and power-efﬁcient architecture. The new contributions to this research are the following: K.R. Krishnaiah et al.

- Creation of ESP32 based home automation system which incorporates cloud  computing to monitor and control real-time data. - Introduction of a multi-sensor system (DHT22, LDR, PIR) that is environmentally  aware and can be adapted to automation. - Intelligent actuation means the accomplishment of energy efﬁciency, which will cut  down the total power consumption by about 18 percent. - Full performance analysis with low latency and system reliability at minimum under  continuous load.

This paper is organized in the following manner: Section 2 will provide the literature review of the latest developments in the ﬁeld of the IoT-based home automation. Section 3 speciﬁes the proposed system architecture and system design principles. Section 4 explains hardware and software implementation of the ESP32 based system. Section 5 contains the discussion of the experimental ﬁndings and performance an evaluation, showing the accuracy and efﬁciency of the system. Section 6 is the conclusion of the paper and Sect. 7 gives future research directions.

## 2 **Literature Review **

The ﬁeld of home automation based on the IoT-enabled systems has experienced substantial research in the last few years with emphasis on energy use, scalability, and costefﬁciency. The growing accessibility of microcontrollers like ESP8266 and ESP32 has facilitated the creation of low-cost, wireless automation frameworks capable of tracking and controlling appliances via the use of the cloud. Addow et al. \[ 5 \] suggested a cheap IoT based home automation model that focuses on the sustainability in urban areas in relation to energy saving and convenience in setup in developing nations. Their research revealed that it is possible to conduct automation systems at a minimum cost, and they are still reliable in operation.

The article by Serepas et al. \[ 6 \] was a lightweight embedded IoT gateway created around ESP32 microcontrollers and advantages the use of minimized resources and local processing to cut down on network trafﬁc. Here, in the same vein, Kaur et al. \[ 7 \]  developed an intelligent home automation system that incorporated ESP32 and cloud services showing better performance and compatibility of devices. All these works highlight the increased signiﬁcance of ESP32 as one of the preferred microcontrollers with integrated Wi-Fi chip, low-power consumption, and excellent integration with IoT s ystems.

Maduka et al. \[ 8 \] adopted a cloud-integrated home automation with a good emphasis on scalability, real-time control data visualization, whereas Baliyan et al. \[ 9 \]  aimed at developing cost-effective systems that would sustain energy-saving mechanisms by using smart scheduling. In addition, Mishra et al. \[ 10 \] applied the IoT to sustainable agricultural monitoring, which shows how the same architecture could be ﬂexed to energy-efﬁcient smart homes.

Santhikiran et al. \[ 11 \] presented smart home systems ESPRainmaker-based systems which simplify the conﬁguration of devices and lower the latency by directly connecting them to the cloud. Obayuwana et al. \[ 12 \] focused on IoT-based ﬁre detection solutions, improving the safety and preventive maintenance of the house by offering economical solutions. Taken together, these studies demonstrate how home automation technologies

## 3 **System Architecture and Design **

## The system architecture described in the ESP32-based home automation system is cre

ated to ensure the smooth communication between the sensors, actuators, and the cloudbased IoT solutions. The structure allows real-time monitoring, effective communication, and smart decision-making of the control over home appliances. It is based on the principles of modularity, scalability, and cost-efﬁciency and can be adapted to small and large-scale smart home settings.

## The system has three major layers, which include sensing layer, control layer, and

cloud interface layer. The sensing layer contains various smart sensors which include, K.R. Krishnaiah et al.

the DHT22 which can measure temperature and humidity, the LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) which is able to sense the intensity of ambient light and the PIR (Passive Infrared) sensor which is able to sensing motion. These sensors constantly gather realtime environmental data and communicate the same to the control layer to analyse. The control layer is an ESP32 microcontroller-based control layer which serves as the central processing unit that interprets sensor data, performs control algorithms, and handles data communication via an inbuilt Wi-Fi module. Cloud interface layer also enables the aspects of data visualization, remote control, and automated decision execution, which are implemented using IoT platforms (ThingSpeak and Blynk).

The ES32 based home automation system system architecture is shown in Fig. 1.  It shows how the ESP32 microcontroller, different sensors and actuators and cloud services interact. The sensors are connected to the ESP32 by analog and digital pins where they send all the environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, light intensity, and motion detection signals. Using this information, the ESP32 can run control code to automate appliances e.g. lights, fans or alarm clocks using relay modules. The sensor data obtained is sent to concurrently the cloud to be stored, analyzed, and visualized. Figure 1 shows that the users may interact in real-time and monitor home devices remotely via a mobile or web dashboard, which guarantees high user convenience and the ability to control it.

One of the greatest elements of the design of the proposed system is energy efﬁciency. The ESP32 has low power states when idle and is also capable of event-driven wake-up functions when sensors are active. This design consumes less energy that is not needed and it is responsive. The data provided by the DHT22 sensor can be used to streamline the use of appliances, such as fans are turned on when the temperature is too high and lights are switched on in accordance with LDRs. The PIR sensor also contributes towards saving of energy by turning off appliances when rooms are not used. These adaptive control measures help to achieve a signiﬁcant decrease in the total energy consumption.

The ESP32-cloud server communication protocol is based on the MQTT and HTTP communication protocols, which will guarantee the lightweight, stable, and high-speed data transfer. The cloud integration enables the system to keep logs and do analytics and even take some actions based on predictive conditions. In addition, mobile app usage increases accessibility of the users, allowing them to override the system manually, and get real-time notiﬁcations about motion detection or environmental variations.

The modular design also allows the system to be expanded without reconﬁguring at all, and adding more sensors or control devices. The scalability aspect enables the framework to develop to an entire smart home ecosystem to facilitate security, environmental control, and energy management. To conclude, the proposed architecture is an efﬁcient way to integrate sensing and processing with cloud intelligence when ESP32 microcontroller is taken as the main node. The design is not only capable of providing real time automation and decision making based on data but the design also ensures low cost, high reliability, and energy efﬁciency making it a sustainable and practical solution to a modern smart home.

## 4 **Hardware and Software Implementation **

Home automation system implementation is a proposed system that consists of hardware and software designed to provide real-time monitoring, high reliability, and simpliﬁed deployment. The implementation is a combination of low-cost hardware and versatile cloud-based software platforms to create intelligent automation with low-latency and energy-consumption.

The ESP32 microcontroller is the central processing unit and the control unit embedded into the hardware architecture. ESP32 has been chosen because it has a dual core processor, embedded Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips and low power management capabilities thus making it the perfect choice in IoT-based smart home applications. The sensors that have been linked with the ESP32 are DHT22 sensor, which measures both temperature and humidity, the LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) sensor that detects the ambient light intensity, and the PIR (Passive Infrared) sensor that detects movement. All of these sensors are connected to the ESP32 via GPIO pins, which makes it possible to collect the data correctly and provide a response to the environmental changes in real-time.

The actuators or output devices consist of relays and LEDs, which are controlled depending on the control logic, which is set in the ESP32 ﬁrmware. The relay module permits the system to toggle the high voltage appliances like lights, fans or alarm safely. Also, power regulation circuitry is provided to maintain the voltage levels of the sensors and the ESP32 board constant, which prevents the system to be affected by electrical ﬂuctuations.

The hardware component connections and pin arrangement in the system are shown in Fig. 2. It illustrates the connection of the sensors and actuators to the ESP32 microcontroller such as power supply and communication interfaces. The DHT22 sensor has been connected to a digital pin to send the humidity and temperature values, the LDR sensor to an analog input to detect the lights of different intensity and this sensor and the PIR sensor have been connected to a digital signal where the sensor transmits the digital K.R. Krishnaiah et al.

signal on detecting the motion. The relay driver circuit can be powered by the ESP32 GPIO pins and it is used to switch on and off the connected household appliances. The general wiring arrangement, as illustrated in Fig. 2, is small and modular and hence easily replicable and expandable in the future.

The software implementation of the system is made on the Arduino IDE on ESP32 board support libraries. The code is written in C/C++, with Wi-Fi communication and sensor data processing and cloud integration libraries. The ESP32 can be connected to the local Wi-Fi network and send data to the cloud servers via HTTP and MQTT protocols to ensure a high level of data exchange. The program reads sensor data in the background and runs automation on the sensor data, as well as continuously updating the cloud dashboard.

The ﬂowchart of software implementation as illustrated in Fig. 3 is the working logic of the system. When the ESP32 is initializing, it connects to the Wi-Fi and sets up the sensors. The program then goes into a continuous monitoring loop, and it reads the data of DHT22, LDR, and PIR sensors. The control logic switches appliances on or off by use of relays, which are based on predetermined settings. At the same time, the obtained information is sent to the cloud solution where it is stored and visualized. The error-handling routines are also mentioned in Fig. 3, and it is necessary to guarantee the system stability in case of communication breakdowns or sensor malfunctioning.

The selected clouds in this implementation are ThingSpeak and Blynk, which offer convenient dashboards which can be used to visualize real-time sensor data. Through mobile or web apps, users are able to track the humidity, temperature, light intensity and motion detection events and even control devices remotely. This hardware stability and software adaptability makes it a durable, responsive and energy saving home automation system that can be operated continuously and autonomously.

## 5 **Experimental Results and Discussion **

In order to test the functioning of the proposed ESP32-based home automation system, a complete collection of experiments in controlled conditions in a residential setting was conducted. The parameters that were tested with the system include temperature, humidity, ambient light intensity, motion detection accuracy, response time and the energy efﬁciency. Tests were conducted across several observation time intervals to conﬁrm reliability, real time responsiveness and energy saving performance.

Figure 4(a) shows the real time measurements of the humidity using the DHT22 sensor in eight hours of monitoring. The humidity was observed to be in the range of 52-68 and the regular level of environmental tracking was observed. Figure 4(a) showed that the system was able to sustain a constant surveillance without losing data or drastic ﬂuctuations shown by the stable curve. This stability goes to show that the K.R. Krishnaiah et al.

sensor integration and data acquisition subsystems of the ESP32 system work well and can be used effectively even over an extended period of work.

Figure 4(b) shows the temperature changes recorded at the same period of test. The DHT22 sensor was capable of registering slow changes in ambient temperature between 24 o C and 28 o C. Figure 4(b) indicates that the sensor calibration and realtime information transfer between the ESP32 and the cloud dashboard is precise as indicated by the smooth pattern of variation. These ﬁndings conﬁrm that the system can be applied to adaptive climate control applications, i.e. appliances like air conditioners or exhaust fans can be activated automatically depending on the temperature sensitivities.

The light intensity data, presented in Fig. 4(c), is the readings of the sensor of LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) sensor during a full day-night cycle. The values were high in the daytime (8001000 Lux) and low at night (200400 Lux) and progressively rose later in the sunrise. This data was well exploited by the system to do automated lighting in that, during low ambient light, it would turn lights on and when there is bright light, it will turn them off. The dynamics in Fig. 4(c) prove that the system is able to accommodate dynamic changes in the environment to achieve optimal energy consumption.

In Fig. 4(d), a bar chart of the motion detects by the PIR sensor after every two hours during a period of ten hours is plotted. The maximum propensity was observed in the 4 6 hours interval with 18 events which constitute human motion at the peak of the monitored area. The system was able to capture and store all the motion events at zero false negatives which afﬁrmed the accuracy and responsiveness of the PIR sensor integration. This functionality is needed in applications with automated security systems or appliances which are controlled by occupancy.

Figure 5 is a comparative analysis of the responsiveness of the system that shows the average response time of different operations, including sensor data acquisition, device actuation, and cloud synchronization. ESP32 system demonstrated an average response time of less than 2 seconds and this implies a low level of latency even when numerous tasks were running simultaneously. This fast response testiﬁes to the effectiveness of MQTT and HTTP communication protocols introduced in the system. In practice, low response latency guarantees that user command and sensor-driven events are performed virtually immediately, which enhances the overall user experience.

One of the evaluation parameters that are considered to be critical, energy efﬁciency was evaluated using the comparison of power consumption against traditional manual control systems. The comparison of the power consumption is provided in Fig. 6, where it is indicated that the proposed system was able to reduce the energy consumption by about 18%. This has been made possible by the adaptive automation algorithms that turn off the devices when no one is using them or when there is sufﬁcient lighting in the room. The proposed design has the power optimization capability, which illustrates the environmental and economic beneﬁts of the proposed design, contributing to sustainable smart living solutions.

The results of the experiments conducted in Figs. 4(a), 5 and 6 all testify to the fact that the proposed ESP32-based system manages to incorporate a variety of sensors and actuators into one single yet trustworthy system. The effectiveness of the hardwaresoftware co-design is conﬁrmed by the stability of sensor data, quick activation reaction and the energy efﬁciency of the operations. ## 6 **Conclusion **

The paper introduces the design and deployment of an affordable, cloud-based home automation system powered by an ESP32 microcontroller to monitor and control appliances at home in real-time. The system was effective in integrating various sensors - DHT22, LDR and PIR to measure the environmental and motion parameters with great precision. Users can remotely monitor the environment and remotely control devices

Implementation of a Cost-Effective Home Automation System Using

## remotely through cloud connectivity via platforms like ThingSpeak and Blynk. The per

formance of the experimental analysis was high with consistent humidity measurements ranging between 52% 68, and consistent temperature measurements ranging between 24C to 28C and consistent motion detection of zero false negatives. Besides, the system had an average Response Time of less than two seconds and consumed less energy by about 18 percent as compared to conventional systems. These ﬁndings conﬁrm that the proposed ESP32-based IoT system can be considered a viable, scalable, and energy-efﬁcient system to use in the current smart home setting.

## 7 **Future Scope **

## Although the automation and energy optimization of the proposed system is achieved

successfully in real-time, it can be extended in the future. By incorporating machine learning predictive control algorithms with adaptive energy management algorithms, the system would be able to learn user behavior and automatically adapt the patterns of appliance use. Voice-assisted control and AI-based anomaly detection could also be added to future implementations to provide the user with an improved experience and security. Also, using edge computing may lead to the reduction of relying on cloud connectivity and enhance the speed of making local decisions. Expanding the system to accommodate multi-node distributed networks would turn single smart homes into a network of smart communities that can help bring about sustainable and intelligent urban living.
